after.title: Working assumptions (Foreman, challenge these)
after.text:
- Human controls 1 kid; 3 AI teammates vs 4 AI rivals (8 kids total).
- Short matches: best of 3 rounds, ~3 min each. Hit kids get 'chilled' and sit out at the cocoa stand.
- Credits earned from hits/round wins; spent between rounds in a shop. Final score is NOT credits (spending shouldn't hurt score).
- Controls target: move + aim/throw + one build key. If it needs more, cut something.

summary: added section “Hook: Snow Day (Creative v0)”

after.title: Hook: Snow Day (Creative v0)
after.text:
THE HOOK — Two streets, one sledding hill, and the streetlights are about to come on.

- WIN: hold the toboggan at the top of the hill. Round ends when the lights flicker on; most hill-time wins. No elimination — a chilled kid warms up at the cocoa stand ~5s and jogs back.
- TONE: cozy = warm, silly, low stakes. Every upgrade is junk a kid could find in a garage or kitchen. If it looks like a weapon ad, cut it.
- FIRST 30s: the whistle, then everybody sprints up the hill. No shop, no tutorial — teach by racing.
- REPLAY: the last 20 seconds are a panic because you can watch the sky go orange.

summary: added “7. Throwing: aim a spot, the arc is geo…” to Core loop rules — Systems (implement exactly)

after.label: 7. Throwing: aim a spot, the arc is geometry
after.text:
No tap/hold, no lob button. Stick aims a landing ring; release throws at it.
- Flight time = 0.3s + 0.12s per metre. Arc apex grows with distance by itself.
- Wall is 1.5m tall. A throw only clears it if the ball is above 1.5m as it passes the wall — which only happens for rings ~5m+ beyond it. So walls stop the close game and nothing else.
- Ice chunk: half flight time, sweeps through walls (breaks them), range 6m.
- Leaf blower: double flight time and apex, range 14m — slow enough to walk out of.
- READABILITY (Art's answer, systems side): the ground is the readout. The landing ring (r 0.8m) is visible to everyone the moment a throw is committed, and the ball casts a shadow dot on the snow. A 1.3s lob is dodgeable because the ring sits there the whole flight. No HUD.
after.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Snow Day visual identity
entries.text: Chunky storybook miniatures: oversized mittens, expressive scarf tails, carved snowbanks, warm porch windows against blue-violet snow. Chestnut = burnt orange + horizontal scarf bands; Maple = deep teal + chevrons. Shapes/patterns distinguish teams without color. Human has a small white overhead chevron; sled carrier has a pennant above heads and a scarf outline. Keep trees/buildings out of the playable foreground.

entries.label: Aim feedback must describe real collisions
entries.text: PROPOSAL: local aim preview shows a thin dotted ground path and destination; if a wall intercepts, terminate at the wall with a blunt stop mark. Committed enemy throws get a broken coral landing bracket plus moving ground shadow; friendly throws use small teal ticks. No filled danger discs: a projectile is not an explosion. Incoming balls need dark undersides + short bright streaks against snow. Hide distant friendly prediction clutter. Systems must clarify whether balls hit kids in flight or only at landing; landing rings alone do not communicate mid-flight hits.

after.label: 5. Hits: first contact or landing ring? (Art's question)
after.text: RULING I'd defend: a ball hits (a) the first kid it touches in flight, or (b) anyone standing inside the landing ring at touchdown. No friendly fire. This is affordable because flat throws are over in ~0.4s at close range — reflex, and the ball is right there on screen — while every long throw is a slow lob that stays above head height until its own ring. So the ground ring IS the honest warning for anything slow enough to react to, and Art needs no extra mid-flight warning. Landing-only hits would make players watch balls pass through their kid and call it broken.

after.text:

- Win: king-of-the-hill with the toboggan (Systems rules 1–8).
- No elimination: chilled kid warms up at a mid-hill cocoa stand, ~8s total downtime.
- No currency. Garage draft between rounds: pick 1 of 2 junk cards, lasts the match.
- Cards: ice chunk, leaf blower, cocoa thermos. Cards change your ball only; everyone keeps the wall key.
- Hits: first kid touched below head height in flight, or anyone in the ring at touchdown. No friendly fire.
- Controls: move, aim/throw, wall. Throw doubles as sled handoff.

before.text:
The arc should be a property of the ball, not a mode on the key. Tap always throws, no wind-up:
- Snowball: flat and fast up close, auto-lobs at long range (slow, easy to step out from under).

entries.text: Priority 1: grab the sled whenever it is free or the enemy carrier is chilled. Then take the shortest legal path to the crown (ridge, not up the steep face). Throws only if the sled has been off the crown 5s. Never builds. She is the clock — the human's job is stopping her.

entries.label: Pockets — she never gets close
entries.text: Holds 6-10m from the nearest enemy, always faces the enemy carrier, fires the slow lob over the scrum, retreats immediately if anyone closes inside 5m. Never picks up the sled (fallback grab only). She is why escorts get pelted and must choose.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Brick — he builds the road
entries.text: Every 12s places a wall between his carrier and the nearest threat; max 3 alive. No sled in play = stands 2m in front of the carrier as a walking shield. Throws only when no build is available. He is the reason killing Brick first is a real tactic.

entries.label: Copycat — he does what you just did

before.text: Do NOT assume two narrow approaches cure overlap: funnels can stack eight silhouettes and make lob camping stronger. Greybox A: broad flat saddle, same 4m-radius scoring crown, two approaches each at least 3 kid-widths, low shoulders and open foreground. B: narrow two-approach ridge, same travel times/crown/rules. after.label: Crown scrum — compare broad saddle vs narrow ridge (Art + QA)
after.text:
Do NOT assume two narrow approaches cure overlap: funnels can stack eight silhouettes and make lob camping stronger. Greybox A: broad flat saddle, same 4m-radius scoring crown, two approaches each at least 3 kid-widths, low shoulders and open foreground. B: narrow two-approach ridge, same travel times/crown/rules. Same eight-bot seed, 4 concurrent throws, 720p; test finding human/carrier and spotting escape route within 1s. Log stationary-carrier time too. Prefer A unless B demonstrably wins; no warning-system expansion yet.

QA READ (answers Art): the one-second gate is about silhouettes and eyelines, not about how many approaches there are — so A is the safer bet and it is testable right now: crown shoulders lower than a kid's head, open foreground, and no two bodies overlapping on the crown rim. A can pass with zero extra UI. Build B only if A fails the stationary-carrier log, and remember that log is driven by Pockets' lobs and bot reaction times, not hill shape — don't buy geometry to fix an AI number. If B stacks eight silhouettes on one rim it fails even at 1 second, and we delete it.

author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa
summary: added “8. Dodge chance (30–80%) is a lie the p…” to QA: playtest risks — test these before adding anything

after.label: 8. Dodge chance (30–80%) is a lie the player can feel
after.text: A dice-roll dodge means a ball with a perfect landing ring sometimes misses for no visible reason. The beginner reads it as 'my aim is broken'; the experienced player reads it as 'the bots cheat', stops aiming at Pockets, and the enemy archetype is wasted. FIX: keep ONE number — reaction time 0.25–0.6s. A bot steps out only if it can physically reach the edge of the ring in the time left; otherwise it stands and eats the hit. Dodges become visible movement, hits become earned, and difficulty is still a single slider. Cut the %.

before.label: 5. Hits — RULED: first contact below head height, or ring at touchdown
before.text: RULING I'd defend: a ball hits (a) the first kid it touches in flight, or (b) anyone standing inside the landing ring at touchdown. No friendly fire. This is affordable because flat throws are over in ~0.4s at close range — reflex, and the ball is right there on screen — while every long throw is a slow lob that stays above head height until its own ring. So the ground ring IS the honest warning for anything slow enough to react to, and Art needs no extra mid-flight warning. Landing-only hits would make players watch balls pass through their kid and call it broken.

before.label: Crown scrum — compare broad saddle vs narrow ridge (Art + QA)
before.text:
Do NOT assume two narrow approaches cure overlap: funnels can stack eight silhouettes and make lob camping stronger. Greybox A: broad flat saddle, same 4m-radius scoring crown, two approaches each at least 3 kid-widths, low shoulders and open foreground. B: narrow two-approach ridge, same travel times/crown/rules. Same eight-bot seed, 4 concurrent throws, 720p; test finding human/carrier and spotting escape route within 1s. Log stationary-carrier time too. Prefer A unless B demonstrably wins; no warning-system expansion yet.

QA READ (answers Art): the one-second gate is about silhouettes and eyelines, not about how many approaches there are — so A is the safer bet and it is testable right now: crown shoulders lower than a kid's head, open foreground, and no two bodies overlapping on the crown rim. A can pass with zero extra UI. Build B only if A fails the stationary-carrier log, and remember that log is driven by Pockets' lobs and bot reaction times, not hill shape — don't buy geometry to fix an AI number. If B stacks eight silhouettes on one rim it fails even at 1 second, and we delete it.

after.label: Crown: build greybox A (broad saddle) first

before.title: Decided (Foreman)
before.text:
- 1 human + 3 AI allies vs 4 AI. Best of 3 rounds, 180s each, on 3 hills (yours, theirs, park).

- No elimination: chilled kid warms up at a mid-hill cocoa stand, ~8s total downtime.
- No currency. Garage draft between rounds: pick 1 of 2 junk cards, lasts the match.
- Cards: ice chunk, leaf blower, cocoa thermos. Cards change your ball only; everyone keeps the wall key.
- Hits: first kid touched below head height in flight, or anyone in the ring at touchdown. No friendly fire.

after.title: Decided (Foreman)
after.text:
- 1 human + 3 AI allies vs 4 AI. Best of 3 rounds, 180s each, on 3 hills (yours, theirs, park).

after.title: Greybox bot round — logs and pass/fail (Systems)

entries.label: Record one CSV, one fixed seed
entries.text: Per second: sled state (free / carried + carrier id / on crown) and both scores. Per throw: thrower, ring position, flight time, outcome (hit kid / blocked by wall / landed empty). Per kid: chilled timestamps, time unable to act, distance travelled. Conditions: hill A, 8 bots (human replaced by a bot at the same difficulty), plain snowballs only, no cards, reaction time fixed at the middle value so the round is repeatable.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Pass/fail — does the loop exist
entries.text: Sled on the crown 25-60% of the 180s. Belongs to nobody = nothing to contest; above 60% = king-of-the-hill solved. Changes hands at least 6 times. Longest single hold no more than 25s — longer means camping is confirmed and the fix is geometry or a rule, never another HUD. The 15s idle-slide fires at most once per round.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Pass/fail — are the decisions real
entries.text: Each team chilled 6-12 times per round (fewer = throwing is pointless). Hit rate from 6-10m on a moving kid 35-60%: under 25% the lob is unfair, over 70% dodging is decoration. At least half of all misses must be the target physically stepping out of the ring — that proves the ring is the verb and not a graphic. Every bot chilled at least once, none more than 4 times. Human unable to act under 15% of round 1.

before.label: 10. Does the draft have a right answer?
before.text: Intended triangle: ice chunk beats wall users, leaf blower is the only ball that clears a 1.5m wall, thermos beats attrition. Risk: chunk is simply the best ball (fast, breaks what covers you) while a 4s lob is walked out of, making 2 of 3 picks a formality and the 'foreign hill' feel like a tax. CHEAPEST FIX if chunk dominates: make walls cheaper for everyone (Brick 12s → 8s cadence) rather than buffing lob damage — repair the draft by making walls matter, not by adding numbers.
before.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

after.label: 10. Draft: is the shovel the only answer now?
after.text: New triangle: chunk breaks walls, blower clears them, shovel makes more of them. The risk has flipped — the shovel is the only card that gives MOBILE cover, and since flat throws are most of the game, a kid who walks up the hill behind a wall he can re-plant may be untouchable from the front. If it dominates, repair it by making the wall break more cheaply (chunk range 6m → 7m) rather than nerfing the shovel into a second chunk. TEST at cards phase: 20 seeded bot rounds per card, log each card's win rate and hits taken per round; delete any card outside 40–60%.
after.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

after.label: 11. Shovel: plant it at your feet — kills Art's flicker
after.text: Answer to Art's real risk: the flicker only exists because placement is remote (aim anywhere, wall appears). Cheapest fix, and the cozier fantasy: a shovel wall is planted where YOU stand, instantly and free, one at a time, with a ~3s cooldown between plants. Broken wall still eats the shared 8s. So mobile cover means physically carrying your cover up the hill — no teleport-shield, no frame-by-frame re-plant, no aim UI, and it can't be planted on the crown (rule 8). TEST: log wall plants per 10s; more than 1 average means we built a flickering shield and misread it as a card.

before.text:
- 1 human + 3 AI allies vs 4 AI. Best of 3 rounds, 180s each, on 3 hills (yours, theirs, park).

after.title: Progression: nothing carries over (Creative, one line)
after.text:
Nothing carries over between matches. No unlocks, no currency, no stats — a match (3 rounds, three hills, ~10 min) is already a full session, and the draft and the bot mix give it replay room.

What does carry is the story:
- THE FLAG. The hill keeps the winner's pennant for the rest of the session, so match 2 starts with someone else's colours on your crown. One texture, infinite grudges.
- The ladder doesn't grow you, it grows the rivals: the same four obsessions in the next street's colours, faster reaction times, same hills. You don't get stronger; you meet worse kids.

Content cost: a scarf palette, not level art.

after.text: Nothing carries between matches: no unlocks, no currency, no stats. The ladder only speeds the rivals up, using the dial we already have — reaction time to a landing ring: street 1 = 0.60s, 2 = 0.50, 3 = 0.45, 4 = 0.40, 5 = 0.35. Same four obsessions, same three hills, same cards on every street; only the scarf colour and that one number change. Losing a match never drops you a street. A cleared street leaves its pennant on the hilltop pole for the rest of the session, so match 2 opens with enemy colours on your crown. after.title: Maple Court's four kids — AI spec as characters

before.label: Behaviour rules (Systems) — implement these, no state trees
before.text:
Beanie: grab the sled when it is free or the enemy carrier is chilled, then shortest legal path to the crown; throws only if the sled has been off the crown 5s; never builds.
Pockets: hold 6-10m from the nearest enemy, face the enemy carrier, lob over the scrum, retreat if anyone gets inside 5m; fallback grabber.
Brick: keeps his ONE wall (same rules as the player) between his carrier and the nearest threat; rebuilds when it breaks. With no sled in play, a walking shield 2m ahead of the carrier.
Copycat: 2s after the human acts, repeat that action type; never initiates.
Difficulty = ONE number: reaction time to a landing ring (0.25-0.6s). A bot dodges only if it can physically reach the ring edge in time left (QA #8; dice-roll dodge cut).
Fallback carrier when designated one is chilled 3s+: Pockets, Copycat, Brick.
ALLIES (Foreman): Chestnut's 3 bots reuse Beanie/Pockets/Brick logic, but never take the sled from the human. One AI codebase, replaces rule 6's escort logic.

after.title: What a good throw feels like (Creative, hand Systems the number)
after.text:
- A snowball should be a hard flat line that arrives just as the kid flinches. Dodging is something you do BEFORE the ball, not after it.
- So the plain ball travels roughly 0.35s + 0.05s/m: 6m ≈ 0.65s, 8m ≈ 0.75s. A 0.45–0.6s reactor beats that only by a step, which is the exact shot I want in the log — the kid physically moves and the ball skids past their boots.
- The leaf blower keeps the slow old arc (you can walk out of it); that is its price for going over walls. The ice chunk stays flat and fast.
- Facing you = they beat you. Side, back, or busy carrying/building = they cannot. Flanking is the skill, so a plainsnowball range hit rate near 50% is healthy, not broken.
- The thing to protect: a miss must always LOOK like a near miss. Ball visibly skidding past the kid = fine. Ball appearing to pass through them = broken, whatever the math says.

before.label: 7. Throwing: aim a spot, the arc is geometry
before.text:
No tap/hold, no lob button. Stick aims a landing ring; release throws at it.
- Flight time = 0.3s + 0.12s per metre. Arc apex grows with distance by itself.
- Wall is 1.5m tall. A throw only clears it if the ball is above 1.5m as it passes the wall — which only happens for rings ~5m+ beyond it. So walls stop the close game and nothing else.
- Ice chunk: half flight time, sweeps through walls (breaks them), range 6m.
- Leaf blower: double flight time and apex, range 14m — slow enough to walk out of.
- READABILITY (Art's answer, systems side): the ground is the readout. The landing ring (r 0.8m) is visible to everyone the moment a throw is committed, and the ball casts a shadow dot on the snow. A 1.3s lob is dodgeable because the ring sits there the whole flight. No HUD.

after.label: 7. Throwing: aim a spot, the ball is a hard line
after.text:
No tap/hold. Stick aims a landing ring (r 0.8m); release throws at it.
- Plain snowball: 0.35s + 0.05s/m (6m = 0.65s, 10m = 0.85s). Flat and fast. This is the default verb and it must read as a hard line, not a lob.
- Ice chunk: 0.25s + 0.03s/m, flat, sweeps through walls (breaks them), 6m.
- Leaf blower: 0.50s + 0.12s/m (10m = 1.7s), high apex, clears walls, 14m. Slow on purpose — that is the price of going over.
- A 1.5m wall is only cleared by a ball already above 1.5m as it passes it.
- Ring visible to everyone from the moment of commitment; the ball carries a shadow dot on the snow.

after.label: Pass/fail — are the decisions real (hit math rerun)
after.text:
Time to clear a ring = reaction (0.60/0.50/0.45s) + 0.25s to step 0.8m at human speed + 0.1s slop = 0.95s / 0.85s / 0.80s.
The ball must win the obvious case: a free, aware, facing kid at 6-10m is hit at least 60% of the time (ball 0.65-0.85s, they need 0.95s at street 1). Under 50% here, the flight time is wrong, not the bots. At 10m street 3 they can just clear it — long range gets harder exactly as the player gets better.
Carrier or builder: ~100%, they cannot dodge by rule.
Thrown from outside the ~120° front arc: ~100%.
Overall match hit rate 30-45%, because most throws go into bad angles. Above 60% the bots are blind; below 25% that hill has no flanking route — fix the geometry.
Each team chilled 6-12 times a round; every bot at least once, none more than 4 times.
Readable miss: at least 80% of misses pass within 1.2m of the kid. A ball crossing through a body is a collision bug, not a miss.

summary: edited section “What a good throw feels like (Creative)”

before.title: What a good throw feels like (Creative, hand Systems the number)
before.text:
- A snowball should be a hard flat line that arrives just as the kid flinches. Dodging is something you do BEFORE the ball, not after it.
- So the plain ball travels roughly 0.35s + 0.05s/m: 6m ≈ 0.65s, 8m ≈ 0.75s. A 0.45–0.6s reactor beats that only by a step, which is the exact shot I want in the log — the kid physically moves and the ball skids past their boots.
- The leaf blower keeps the slow old arc (you can walk out of it); that is its price for going over walls. The ice chunk stays flat and fast.
- Facing you = they beat you. Side, back, or busy carrying/building = they cannot. Flanking is the skill, so a plainsnowball range hit rate near 50% is healthy, not broken.
- The thing to protect: a miss must always LOOK like a near miss. Ball visibly skidding past the kid = fine. Ball appearing to pass through them = broken, whatever the math says.

after.title: What a good throw feels like (Creative)
after.text: A snowball is a hard flat line (0.35s + 0.05s/m) that arrives just as the kid flinches. A free, watching kid at 6–10m gets hit ≥60% of the time — reflex-dodging is NOT the skill. 1) The skill is the angle: a kid facing you sees it; a kid at your side, from behind, or busy carrying/building cannot. Match-wide 30–45% hit rate is healthy because most throws come from bad angles. 2) A plain ball NEVER clears a wall — walls are the reason to move. The leaf blower (0.50s + 0.12s/m) is the only slow, walk-out-of-it arc. 3) Protect this: a miss must look like a near miss — ball skidding past the boots, never through them; ≥80% of misses pass within 1.2m.

before.title: Decided (Foreman)
before.text:
- 1 human + 3 AI allies vs 4 AI. Best of 3 rounds, 180s each, on 3 hills (yours, theirs, park).
- Win: king-of-the-hill with the toboggan (Systems rules 1–10). Round 1 sled starts beside the human. Crown = broad saddle (greybox A). Sudden death capped at 60s.
- No elimination: chilled kid warms up at a cocoa stand at the side of the hill, ~8s total, out of play while there.
- Garage draft (human only) before rounds 2 and 3: pick 1 of 2, hold one card.
- Plain snowball = fast flat line, never clears a wall. Cards: ice chunk (breaks walls), leaf blower (slow lob over walls), snow shovel (instant wall at your feet). Everyone has the wall key, one wall each.
- Hits: first kid touched below head height in flight, or anyone in the ring at touchdown. No friendly fire. Hit/miss/splat readable as aftermath.
- AI: 4 archetypes, fair-bot rule (committed rings in facing arc only). Pockets uses the blower. Difficulty = reaction 0.45–0.60s + team mix.
- Session: 3-street ladder, nothing carries over.
- Controls: move, aim/throw, wall. Throw doubles as sled handoff.

RULESET FROZEN. Changes now come only from greybox data or the human session.
BUILD ORDER: 1) greybox hill A, 8 bots, plain snowballs + Pockets' blower + ring + first-contact hits + wall, placeholder silhouettes. Run the bot CSV, then QA's 3-first-timer session + Art's clip test. 2) cards. 3) art.

before.label: Pass/fail — are the decisions real (hit math rerun)
before.text:
Time to clear a ring = reaction (0.60/0.50/0.45s) + 0.25s to step 0.8m at human speed + 0.1s slop = 0.95s / 0.85s / 0.80s.
The ball must win the obvious case: a free, aware, facing kid at 6-10m is hit at least 60% of the time (ball 0.65-0.85s, they need 0.95s at street 1). Under 50% here, the flight time is wrong, not the bots. At 10m street 3 they can just clear it — long range gets harder exactly as the player gets better.
Carrier or builder: ~100%, they cannot dodge by rule.
Thrown from outside the ~120° front arc: ~100%.
Overall match hit rate 30-45%, because most throws go into bad angles. Above 60% the bots are blind; below 25% that hill has no flanking route — fix the geometry.
Each team chilled 6-12 times a round; every bot at least once, none more than 4 times.
Readable miss: at least 80% of misses pass within 1.2m of the kid. A ball crossing through a body is a collision bug, not a miss.

after.label: 19. Rule 2 (idle sled slides home) is the first rule I'd delete
after.text: It exists to kill a 0-0 turtle, but rule 8 already stops camping and rule 1's carrier has no reason to abandon the sled. In practice it fires when eight kids are fighting around a dropped sled, and a sled that slides away mid-fight reads as a bug and hands one side a free reset. Systems' own log expects it to fire 'at most once per round' — a rule that fires once is a rule nobody learns. DECISION RULE: if the log shows it firing 0 times, delete it and gain a rule back; if it fires 2+, it's actively confusing the fight and should be a shouted countdown the kids can see instead of a silent 15s timer.

before.label: 19. Rule 2 (idle sled slides home) is the first rule I'd delete
before.text: It exists to kill a 0-0 turtle, but rule 8 already stops camping and rule 1's carrier has no reason to abandon the sled. In practice it fires when eight kids are fighting around a dropped sled, and a sled that slides away mid-fight reads as a bug and hands one side a free reset. Systems' own log expects it to fire 'at most once per round' — a rule that fires once is a rule nobody learns. DECISION RULE: if the log shows it firing 0 times, delete it and gain a rule back; if it fires 2+, it's actively confusing the fight and should be a shouted countdown the kids can see instead of a silent 15s timer.

before.label: Identity must survive 48px (Creative correction to the visual spec)
before.text: At 48px kids, oversized mittens and face detail are texture, not identity — nobody in the gate will see them. Identity carriers, in priority order: 1) head shape (beanie / hood / bare head), 2) team block colour plus scarf pattern (orange bands vs teal chevrons), 3) stance (Beanie leans forward, Brick sits low, Pockets stands tall), 4) the sled pennant — the only object with a silhouette of its own. Spend the storybook charm on the WORLD: snow banks, porch lights, chimney smoke, the sky dimming in visible steps. Cut any kid detail we cannot read at 48px; that is where the art budget should NOT go.

after.title: Greybox verdict rules (QA) — decide before we look
after.text:
Three first-timers, no coaching, one full match on hill A, final camera framing, ending in place (dusk steps, lights on, 20s countdown).

Observables, in order: 1) touches the sled within 20s of the whistle; 2) hands off before minute 5; 3) presses the wall key unprompted in round 1; 4) says who is winning at 60s and at 150s; 5) ever glances at the sky for time; 6) asks for another round.

One decision per failure, agreed now:
- never touches the sled → the objective isn't teaching itself: cut a rule or move a spawn, never add a prompt.
- never hands off → the handoff is invisible: fix the ally wave, don't explain it with text.
- never builds → walls are decoration: cut the wall key and the shovel card together, don't add a tutorial.
- can't say who's winning → the score strip is wrong; the tester is not.
- never looks at the sky → the sky is decoration, keep the countdown and give the dusk back to the atmosphere.
- doesn't ask for another round → the round is too long or too quiet: drop 180s to 120s before adding anything.

n=3 proves confusion, not fun. Three testers can only pass/fail the six observables above; calling it fun needs the host playing a whole match with people. Write down every unprompted sentence a tester says — that's where the real defects are.

author: claude
summary: edited section “Decided (Foreman)”

before.title: Decided (Foreman)
before.text:
- 1 human + 3 AI allies vs 4 AI. Best of 3 rounds, 180s each, on 3 hills (yours, theirs, park).
- Win: king-of-the-hill with the toboggan (Systems rules 1–12). Round 1 sled starts beside the human; rounds 2–3 neutral. Crown = same flat 4m saddle on every hill. Tied round → sudden death, capped 60s.
- Camera: one fixed iso shot, whole ~26m hill on screen, kids ~48px at 720p. No pan.
- No elimination: chilled kid warms up at a cocoa stand at the side of the hill, ~8s total, out of play while there.
- Garage draft (human only) before rounds 2 and 3: pick 1 of 2, hold one card.
- Plain snowball = fast flat line, never clears a wall. Cards: ice chunk (breaks walls), leaf blower (slow lob over walls), snow shovel (instant wall at your feet). Everyone has the wall key, one wall each.
- Hits: first kid touched below head height in flight, or anyone in the ring at touchdown. One hit chills. No friendly fire. Hit/miss/splat readable as aftermath.
- AI: 4 archetypes, fair-bot rule (committed rings in facing arc only). Pockets uses the blower. Difficulty = reaction 0.45–0.60s + team mix.
- Session: 3-street ladder, nothing carries over.
- Controls: move, aim/throw, wall. Throw doubles as sled handoff.

RULESET FROZEN. Changes now come only from greybox data or the human session.
BUILD ORDER: 1) greybox hill A, 8 bots, plain snowballs + Pockets' blower + ring + first-contact hits + wall, placeholder silhouettes, final camera. Run the bot CSV, then QA's 3-first-timer session + Art's clip test. 2) cards. 3) art.

after.text:
**Board audit: wargames.** 30 problems found. Each line gives where it is, then the problem.

**Contradictions**
1. **Snowball fight › "Players"** says "4 AI players + one human". The Brief says 1 human + 3 AI allies vs 4 AI, which is 7 bots.
2. **Maple › "Beanie" vs "Behaviour rules"**: the character entry says Beanie "never throws". The behaviour rule says he throws if the sled has been off the crown for 5s.
3. **Maple › "Brick" vs "Behaviour rules"**: Brick "never carries", but the fallback-carrier order lists Pockets, Copycat, *Brick*.
4. **Maple › "Pockets"**: the label says "never within 6m" but the behaviour rule makes him retreat only inside 5m. "Won't chase the sled" also clashes with "fallback grabber".
5. **Rule 6 vs ally Brick**: ally Brick walks 2m ahead of the carrier, so he will often be the ally within 6m waving for the sled. Brick never carries, so the rules don't say what happens if the human hands him the sled.
6. **Rule 8 vs Brick's "walking shield 2m ahead"**: rule 8 bans walls within 2m of the sled. Brick's wall sits exactly on that line.
7. **QA #10**: it says fix a dominant shovel by raising chunk range 6m → 7m, then says "delete any card outside 40–60%". Systems' "Cards phase" says "deleted, not nerfed". These can't all hold.
8. **QA #17 (cocoa stand)**: it calls the stand "mid-hill", puts kids "on the porch with a mug" and suggests "behind the fence". The Brief and Hook say "at the side of the hill".
9. **Flowchart › "Snow Day whistle"**: "everyone sprints for the hilltop… no upgrades in play yet". The sled starts by the human's porch (round 1) or at the foot of the hill (rounds 2–3), and Pockets has the blower from round 1.
10. **Rule 13 vs picture o_538bb262**: rule 13 says "both hands on the sled", the picture caption says "carried under arm". The busy pose needs one definition.
11. **Verdict rules vs the Brief**: the Verdict asks for "one full match on hill A", but a match is three hills (yours, theirs, park). Cards come in phase 2, so the greybox match also has no draft.

**Numbers that don't add up**
12. **Bot round › "hit math rerun"**: 1280px ÷ 26m ≈ 49px/m, not ~45.
13. **Same entry vs Art › "Readability gate"**: 36px is the ring's *radius* (0.8m). The gate measures "ring *across* its 36px", but the diameter is about 72–79px.
14. **Verdict rules vs CSV**: the verdict splits handoffs at 90s, but the CSV buckets them by minute, and the 60–120s bucket straddles 90s.
15. **Verdict "six or more handoffs" vs Bot pass/fail "changes hands at least 6 times"**: same threshold, different events (shove vs any change of carrier). That makes a passing bot log easy to misread as a reason to cut the clock.

**Gaps**
16. **Bot round CSV (8 bots)**: Chestnut has only three archetypes defined, so the human's slot has no bot spec. And Copycat only copies the human, so with no human it does nothing all run.
17. **Cards-phase tests (QA #10 and Bot "Cards phase")**: per-card win rate comes from bot rounds, but rule 4 says "Bots don't draft". No bot ever holds a card.
18. **Rule 5 vs rule 9**: plant time and placement for the normal wall key aren't specified. Rule 9's "no remote placement" hints the base wall *is* placed remotely.
19. **Rule 10**: what "Next street" does after street 3 is undefined, and the street 2 mix is unstated.
20. **Art › "Readability gate" (flank check)**: it says "each of the four spawns", but spawns are never defined anywhere.
21. **Brief build order says "Art's clip test"**: there are two clip tests (Art's three 1-second clips and QA #15's 60s aftermath clip). It's unclear which is meant.
22. **The "<15% human downtime" threshold** is struck from the CSV (QA #12) and kept in the readability gate. But no human-session test (Verdict rules) actually measures it.
23. **QA #12's human-session checks** include "find the carrier within 1s", which the Verdict rules (the agreed session script) dropped. The two lists overlap but differ.
24. **Flowchart**: there's no card for cocoa stand, draft or ladder. "Sudden death" goes nowhere, "Three hills" doesn't loop back to the whistle, and the "garage draft, then next hill" arrow also fires after round 3.

6. **Rule 8 vs Brick's "walking shield 2m ahead"**: rule 8 bans walls within 2m of the sled. Brick's wall sits exactly on that line.
7. **QA #10**: it says fix a dominant shovel by raising chunk range 6m → 7m, then says "delete any card outside 40–60%". Systems' "Cards phase" says "deleted, not nerfed". These can't all hold.
8. **QA #17 (cocoa stand)**: it calls the stand "mid-hill", puts kids "on the porch with a mug" and suggests "behind the fence". The Brief and Hook say "at the side of the hill".
9. **Flowchart › "Snow Day whistle"**: "everyone sprints for the hilltop… no upgrades in play yet". The sled starts by the human's porch (round 1) or at the foot of the hill (rounds 2–3), and Pockets has the blower from round 1.
10. **Rule 13 vs picture o_538bb262**: rule 13 says "both hands on the sled", the picture caption says "carried under arm". The busy pose needs one definition.
11. **Verdict rules vs the Brief**: the Verdict asks for "one full match on hill A", but a match is three hills (yours, theirs, park). Cards come in phase 2, so the greybox match also has no draft.

15. **Verdict "six or more handoffs" vs Bot pass/fail "changes hands at least 6 times"**: same threshold, different events (shove vs any change of carrier). That makes a passing bot log easy to misread as a reason to cut the clock.

18. **Rule 5 vs rule 9**: plant time and placement for the normal wall key aren't specified. Rule 9's "no remote placement" hints the base wall *is* placed remotely.
19. **Rule 10**: what "Next street" does after street 3 is undefined, and the street 2 mix is unstated.
20. **Art › "Readability gate" (flank check)**: it says "each of the four spawns", but spawns are never defined anywhere.

22. **The "<15% human downtime" threshold** is struck from the CSV (QA #12) and kept in the readability gate. But no human-session test (Verdict rules) actually measures it.
23. **QA #12's human-session checks** include "find the carrier within 1s", which the Verdict rules (the agreed session script) dropped. The two lists overlap but differ.
24. **Flowchart**: there's no card for cocoa stand, draft or ladder. "Sudden death" goes nowhere, "Three hills" doesn't loop back to the whistle, and the "garage draft, then next hill" arrow also fires after round 3.

25. **"Ruleset frozen (saved as v1)"**: v1 was saved at 20:14:12. Rule 11, the Decided section, the Streetlights card, the CSV entry and the Verdict section (added 20:14:34) all changed after that, so v1 is not the current ruleset.
26. **Dangling references**: rule 3 cites QA #16, rule 8 cites "QA risk #2", rule 12 cites QA #18 and the rule-out reason cites QA #19, all deleted. Rule 9 (QA #11) and rule 10 (QA #14) cite items that aren't on the board. "Wall-block share" cites "Foreman's open worry", but the "Open problems" group was deleted.
27. **Snowball fight › "Economy"** is marked SUPERSEDED and still there. "Scoring" cites rule 4 for cutting credits, but rule 4 no longer mentions credits.
28. **Art › "Score: pennant + top strip"** is checked done but still reads "Challenge to QA's accepted fix… PROPOSAL". It also doesn't say what the pennant on a dropped sled shows.
29. **All 5 flowchart cards** are still status "idea" even though the ruleset is frozen.
30. **Brief › "Hook (Creative v0)"** opens with "One sledding hill" while the match is three hills.

before.label: Behaviour rules (Systems) — implement these, no state trees
before.text:
Beanie: grab the sled when free or the enemy carrier is chilled, shortest legal path to the crown; throws only if the sled has been off the crown 5s; never builds.
Pockets: carries the LEAF BLOWER (plain balls are flat now, so this is how he lobs). Holds 6-10m from the nearest enemy, faces the enemy carrier, retreats if anyone gets inside 5m; fallback grabber. Side effect: round 1 teaches the blower card before the first draft.
Brick: keeps his ONE wall (player rules) between his carrier and the nearest threat; rebuilds when it breaks. No sled in play: walking shield 2m ahead of the carrier.
Copycat: 2s after the human acts, repeats that action type; never initiates.
FAIR-BOT RULE: bots react only to COMMITTED rings inside their ~120° facing arc, at human move speed. Carriers and builders don't dodge.
Difficulty = reaction time 0.45-0.60s + team mix (rule 10).
Fallback carrier when designated one is chilled 3s+: Pockets, Copycat, Brick.
ALLIES: Chestnut's 3 bots reuse Beanie/Pockets/Brick logic, never take the sled from the human.
before.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

Brick: never carries or receives the sled. Keeps his ONE wall (rule 5) between his carrier and the nearest threat, outside the crown and ≥2m from the sled (rule 8). While his wall is down, walks 2m ahead of the carrier as a body shield.

before.label: Pass/fail — are the decisions real (hit math rerun)
before.text:
Time to clear a ring = reaction (0.60/0.50/0.45s) + 0.25s to step 0.8m at human speed + 0.1s slop = 0.95s / 0.85s / 0.80s.
The ball must win the obvious case: a free, aware, facing kid at 6-10m is hit at least 60% of the time (ball 0.65-0.85s, they need 0.95s at street 1). Under 50% here, the flight time is wrong, not the bots. At 10m street 3 they can just clear it — long range gets harder exactly as the player gets better.
Carrier or builder: ~100%, they cannot dodge by rule.
Thrown from outside the ~120° front arc: ~100%.
Overall match hit rate 30-45%, because most throws go into bad angles. Above 60% the bots are blind; below 25% that hill has no flanking route — fix the geometry.
Each team chilled 6-12 times a round; every bot at least once, none more than 4 times.
Readable miss: at least 80% of misses pass within 1.2m of the kid. A ball crossing through a body is a collision bug, not a miss.
AT FINAL CAMERA SCALE (26m hill across 1280px, ~45px per metre): the ring is ~36px, a readable miss gap is ~54px, a step-out is ~36px of visible movement. So the log's metres and the gate's pixels are the same measurement — QA and Art are testing one thing, not two.

before.title: Greybox verdict rules (QA) — decide before we look
before.text:
Three first-timers, no coaching, one full match on hill A, final camera framing, ending in place (dusk steps, lights on, 20s countdown).

Watched during the match, nothing asked: 1) touches the sled within 20s of the whistle; 2) hands off before minute 5; 3) presses the wall key unprompted in round 1; 4) says out loud who is winning at 60s and at 150s; 5) asks for another round. Write down their first unprompted complaint, verbatim, with the minute it happened.

Asked only after the match, never during (Art is right that a glance can't be observed): "what told you time was running out?" (sky vs countdown — never inferred), "what was the best moment?", "what were you trying to do when you weren't carrying?"

One decision per failure, agreed now:
- never touches the sled → the objective isn't teaching itself: cut a rule or move a spawn, never add a prompt.
- never hands off → the handoff is invisible: fix the ally wave, don't explain it with text.
- never builds → walls are decoration for a human: cut the human's wall key and the shovel card; Brick keeps his walls.
- can't say who's winning → the score strip is wrong; the tester is not.
- shrugs at another round → do NOT cut the clock yet: read the handoff buckets first. Six or more handoffs, mostly in the first 90s = no middle, and 180 → 120 is the fix. Handoffs still landing near the lights = the ending didn't land and length was never the problem.

AUDIO for session 1: temp audio on — whistle, footstep crunch, sled grab/drop shout, ball release, impact, wall break, lights clunk. No sound at the moment a landing ring appears, so the session stays comparable to the bot log; flanking is the skill and an audible warning from behind would quietly nerf it. That question is answered in session 2, as a variable, not now.

n=3 proves confusion, not fun. Calling it fun needs the host playing a whole match with people.

before.title: Decided (Foreman)
before.text:
- 1 human + 3 AI allies vs 4 AI. Best of 3 rounds, 180s each, on 3 hills (yours, theirs, park).
- Win: king-of-the-hill with the toboggan (Systems rules). Round 1 sled starts beside the human; rounds 2–3 neutral. Crown = same flat 4m saddle on every hill. Tied round → sudden death, capped 60s.
- Camera: one fixed iso shot, whole ~26m hill on screen, kids ~48px at 720p. No pan.
- No elimination: chilled kid warms up at a cocoa stand at the side of the hill, ~8s total, out of play while there.
- Garage draft (human only) before rounds 2 and 3: pick 1 of 2, hold one card.
- Plain snowball = fast flat line, never clears a wall. Cards: ice chunk (breaks walls), leaf blower (slow lob over walls), snow shovel (instant wall at your feet). Everyone has the wall key, one wall each.
- Hits: first kid touched below head height in flight, or anyone in the ring at touchdown. One hit chills. No friendly fire. Hit/miss/splat readable as aftermath.
- AI: 4 archetypes, fair-bot rule (committed rings in facing arc only). Pockets uses the blower. Difficulty = reaction 0.45–0.60s + team mix.
- Session: 3-street ladder, nothing carries over.
- Controls: move, aim/throw, wall. Throw doubles as sled handoff (allies wave for it).

RULESET FROZEN (saved as v1). Changes now come only from greybox data or the human session (see Verdict rules).
BUILD ORDER: 1) greybox hill A: untextured hill, REAL ending: dusk in ≥4 visible steps, porch lights, streetlights at 180s, plus the score strip's 20s countdown. 8 bots, plain snowballs + Pockets' blower + ring + first-contact hits + wall, placeholder silhouettes, final camera. Run the bot CSV as a pacing run only, then the 3-first-timer session + Art's clip test. 2) cards. 3) art.

after.title: Decided (Foreman)

- No elimination: chilled kid warms up at a cocoa stand at the side of the hill, ~8s total, out of play while there.

before.text:
Outstanding Issues:

**Board audit: wargames.** 30 problems found. Each line gives where it is, then the problem.

**Contradictions**
1. **Snowball fight › "Players"** says "4 AI players + one human". The Brief says 1 human + 3 AI allies vs 4 AI, which is 7 bots.
2. **Maple › "Beanie" vs "Behaviour rules"**: the character entry says Beanie "never throws". The behaviour rule says he throws if the sled has been off the crown for 5s.

after.text:
Pip runs straight at a free sled and Scoop backs him up, so a human who spends the whole match lobbing from midfield can still be carried to a win. Nothing in the verdict measures whether the human mattered: the stopwatch only measures downtime, and 'what were you trying to do when you weren't carrying?' is adjacent but not the same question.

FREE FROM THE SAME CSV: crown-seconds per carrier (team + kid id). The human's share of their own team's crown time should be at least 1/3. Also count rounds that reach sudden death — more than 1 in 6 means crown-seconds scoring is too flat, and the fix is scoring, not more sudden death.

ONE SESSION QUESTION: 'what did you do that changed the score?' If they answer with an ally's carry, the human is a spectator.

SMALLEST FIX IF IT FAILS: no new control. When the sled is free within ~6m of the human, allies hold it for 2s and wave (rule 6, already built) instead of grabbing it instantly. That makes the human the protagonist by wanting, not by prompt.

before.title: Greybox verdict rules (QA) — decide before we look
before.text:
Three first-timers, no coaching, one greybox match: first to 2 rounds, every round on hill A, no cards or draft (phase 1), final camera, ending in place (dusk steps, lights on, 20s countdown).

Watched during the match, nothing asked: 1) touches the sled within 20s of the whistle; 2) hands off (rule 6) before minute 5; 3) presses the wall key unprompted in round 1; 4) says out loud who is winning at 60s and at 150s; 5) asks for another match. Write down their first unprompted complaint, verbatim, with the minute.

Stopwatch, per round: seconds the human cannot act — chilled, walking to the stand, waiting there. Carrying the sled is not downtime, it is play. Target under 15% of a round; over 25% means the bench is too long (5s warm-up) or the stand is too far, not that the tester is bad.

Asked only after the match: "what told you time was running out?" (sky vs countdown), "how did you know the sled changed hands?", "did you ever lose sight of the sled or your kid?", "what was the best moment?", "what were you trying to do when you weren't carrying?"

One decision per failure, agreed now:
- never touches the sled → cut a rule or move a spawn, never add a prompt.
- never hands off → fix the ally wave, don't explain it with text.
- never builds → cut the human's wall key and the shovel card; Brick keeps his walls.
- can't say who's winning → the score strip is wrong, not the tester.
- lost the sled on screen → the fixed camera or the pennant has failed; no new HUD layer.
- shrugs at another match → don't cut the clock yet: read POSSESSION CHANGES in 30s buckets (CSV). Most of them before 90s = the round has no middle, 180 → 120. Still coming near the lights = the ending failed, length wasn't the problem.

AUDIO: temp audio on (whistle, footstep crunch, sled grab/drop shout, ball release, impact, wall break, lights clunk). No sound when a landing ring appears. A capture with no temp audio voids the session.

n=3 proves confusion, not fun. Fun verdict = the host playing a whole match.

after.title: Greybox verdict rules (QA) — decide before we look
after.text:
Three first-timers, no coaching, one greybox match: first to 2 rounds, every round on hill A, no cards or draft (phase 1), final camera, ending in place (dusk steps, lights on, 20s countdown).

Watched during the match, nothing asked: 1) touches the sled within 20s of the whistle; 2) hands off (rule 6) before minute 5; 3) presses the wall key unprompted in round 1, and whether a dead second press makes them stop building; 4) says out loud who is winning at 60s and at 150s; 5) asks for another match. Write down their first unprompted complaint, verbatim, with the minute.

Stopwatch, per round: seconds the human cannot act — chilled, walking to the stand, waiting there. Carrying the sled is not downtime, it is play. Target under 15% of a round; over 25% means the bench is too long (5s warm-up) or the stand is too far, not that the tester is bad.

From the same CSV, free: human's share of their team's crown-seconds (want ≥1/3, QA #21) and rounds that reach sudden death (more than 1 in 6 = scoring too flat, QA #21).

Asked only after the match: "what told you time was running out?" (sky vs countdown), "how did you know the sled changed hands?", "did you ever lose sight of the sled or your kid?", "what did you do that changed the score?", "what was the best moment?", "what were you trying to do when you weren't carrying?"

One decision per failure, agreed now:
- never touches the sled → cut a rule or move a spawn, never add a prompt.
- never hands off → fix the ally wave, don't explain it with text.
- never builds → cut the human's wall key and the shovel card; Brick keeps his walls.
- builds once, then stops after a dead second press → the cooldown has no state on screen; add the ghost footprint, no text.
- can't say who's winning → the score strip is wrong, not the tester.
- lost the sled on screen → the fixed camera or the pennant has failed; no new HUD layer.
- wins without ever carrying (share < 1/3) → the allies are the protagonist, not the human: they hold the free sled and wave. No new control.
- shrugs at another match → don't cut the clock yet: read POSSESSION CHANGES in 30s buckets (CSV). Most of them before 90s = the round has no middle, 180 → 120. Still coming near the lights = the ending failed, length wasn't the problem.

AUDIO: temp audio on (whistle, footstep crunch, sled grab/drop shout, ball release, impact, wall break, lights clunk). No sound when a landing ring appears. A capture with no temp audio voids the session.

n=3 proves confusion, not fun. Fun verdict = the host playing a whole match.

In the scrum they are not: the human's own kid is 48px, the waving ally is somewhere near him, and while carrying the throw key does nothing else at all. A missed handoff is completely silent — no toss, no cooldown, no sound — so the player gets no way to learn "too far" from "no one to give it to."

COUNT IT IN THE SESSION, free off the input log: presses of throw while carrying that produce no handoff, before the first successful handoff, and total silent presses per round. 1–2 = the wave taught it. 3+ = the wave is unreadable, and the fix is the wave (ally turns toward the human, arm higher), never a range ring, a number or a tooltip.

Zero presses at all is QA #20's failure, not this one.

before.text:
Outstanding Issues:

**Board audit: wargames.** 30 problems found. Each line gives where it is, then the problem.

**Contradictions**
1. **Snowball fight › "Players"** says "4 AI players + one human". The Brief says 1 human + 3 AI allies vs 4 AI, which is 7 bots.
2. **Maple › "Beanie" vs "Behaviour rules"**: the character entry says Beanie "never throws". The behaviour rule says he throws if the sled has been off the crown for 5s.
3. **Maple › "Brick" vs "Behaviour rules"**: Brick "never carries", but the fallback-carrier order lists Pockets, Copycat, *Brick*.
4. **Maple › "Pockets"**: the label says "never within 6m" but the behaviour rule makes him retreat only inside 5m. "Won't chase the sled" also clashes with "fallback grabber".
5. **Rule 6 vs ally Brick**: ally Brick walks 2m ahead of the carrier, so he will often be the ally within 6m waving for the sled. Brick never carries, so the rules don't say what happens if the human hands him the sled.
6. **Rule 8 vs Brick's "walking shield 2m ahead"**: rule 8 bans walls within 2m of the sled. Brick's wall sits exactly on that line.
7. **QA #10**: it says fix a dominant shovel by raising chunk range 6m → 7m, then says "delete any card outside 40–60%". Systems' "Cards phase" says "deleted, not nerfed". These can't all hold.
8. **QA #17 (cocoa stand)**: it calls the stand "mid-hill", puts kids "on the porch with a mug" and suggests "behind the fence". The Brief and Hook say "at the side of the hill".
9. **Flowchart › "Snow Day whistle"**: "everyone sprints for the hilltop… no upgrades in play yet". The sled starts by the human's porch (round 1) or at the foot of the hill (rounds 2–3), and Pockets has the blower from round 1.
10. **Rule 13 vs picture o_538bb262**: rule 13 says "both hands on the sled", the picture caption says "carried under arm". The busy pose needs one definition.
11. **Verdict rules vs the Brief**: the Verdict asks for "one full match on hill A", but a match is three hills (yours, theirs, park). Cards come in phase 2, so the greybox match also has no draft.

**Numbers that don't add up**
12. **Bot round › "hit math rerun"**: 1280px ÷ 26m ≈ 49px/m, not ~45.
13. **Same entry vs Art › "Readability gate"**: 36px is the ring's *radius* (0.8m). The gate measures "ring *across* its 36px", but the diameter is about 72–79px.
14. **Verdict rules vs CSV**: the verdict splits handoffs at 90s, but the CSV buckets them by minute, and the 60–120s bucket straddles 90s.
15. **Verdict "six or more handoffs" vs Bot pass/fail "changes hands at least 6 times"**: same threshold, different events (shove vs any change of carrier). That makes a passing bot log easy to misread as a reason to cut the clock.

**Gaps**
16. **Bot round CSV (8 bots)**: Chestnut has only three archetypes defined, so the human's slot has no bot spec. And Copycat only copies the human, so with no human it does nothing all run.
17. **Cards-phase tests (QA #10 and Bot "Cards phase")**: per-card win rate comes from bot rounds, but rule 4 says "Bots don't draft". No bot ever holds a card.
18. **Rule 5 vs rule 9**: plant time and placement for the normal wall key aren't specified. Rule 9's "no remote placement" hints the base wall *is* placed remotely.
19. **Rule 10**: what "Next street" does after street 3 is undefined, and the street 2 mix is unstated.
20. **Art › "Readability gate" (flank check)**: it says "each of the four spawns", but spawns are never defined anywhere.
21. **Brief build order says "Art's clip test"**: there are two clip tests (Art's three 1-second clips and QA #15's 60s aftermath clip). It's unclear which is meant.
22. **The "<15% human downtime" threshold** is struck from the CSV (QA #12) and kept in the readability gate. But no human-session test (Verdict rules) actually measures it.
23. **QA #12's human-session checks** include "find the carrier within 1s", which the Verdict rules (the agreed session script) dropped. The two lists overlap but differ.
24. **Flowchart**: there's no card for cocoa stand, draft or ladder. "Sudden death" goes nowhere, "Three hills" doesn't loop back to the whistle, and the "garage draft, then next hill" arrow also fires after round 3.

**Stale items**
25. **"Ruleset frozen (saved as v1)"**: v1 was saved at 20:14:12. Rule 11, the Decided section, the Streetlights card, the CSV entry and the Verdict section (added 20:14:34) all changed after that, so v1 is not the current ruleset.
26. **Dangling references**: rule 3 cites QA #16, rule 8 cites "QA risk #2", rule 12 cites QA #18 and the rule-out reason cites QA #19, all deleted. Rule 9 (QA #11) and rule 10 (QA #14) cite items that aren't on the board. "Wall-block share" cites "Foreman's open worry", but the "Open problems" group was deleted.
27. **Snowball fight › "Economy"** is marked SUPERSEDED and still there. "Scoring" cites rule 4 for cutting credits, but rule 4 no longer mentions credits.
28. **Art › "Score: pennant + top strip"** is checked done but still reads "Challenge to QA's accepted fix… PROPOSAL". It also doesn't say what the pennant on a dropped sled shows.
29. **All 5 flowchart cards** are still status "idea" even though the ruleset is frozen.
30. **Brief › "Hook (Creative v0)"** opens with "One sledding hill" while the match is three hills.

before.label: 21. Who earns the crown seconds — is the human actually in the score?
before.text:
Pip runs straight at a free sled and Scoop backs him up, so a human who spends the whole match lobbing from midfield can still be carried to a win. Nothing in the verdict measures whether the human mattered: the stopwatch only measures downtime, and 'what were you trying to do when you weren't carrying?' is adjacent, not the same question.

FREE FROM THE SAME CSV: crown-seconds per carrier (team + kid id), and rounds that reach sudden death (more than 1 in 6 = crown-seconds scoring is too flat; fix scoring, not sudden death).

CALIBRATION, NOT A GATE (my correction to v4): carry share under 1/3 is a prompt to look closer, not a verdict on its own. A human can be in the score with throws and walls and never carry. So the number only fails when it arrives WITH a weak answer to the question below.

ONE SESSION QUESTION: 'what did you do that changed the score?' If they name only an ally's carry AND the share is under 1/3, the human is a spectator. Both signals together, then decide.

SMALLEST FIX IF BOTH FAIL: not 6b (ruled out — it makes Pip refuse a loose sled in the opening seconds and breaks Beanie's character). Move the round 2–3 centre sled 1.5m onto Chestnut's side of dead centre. Invisible, no bot rule, no animation, and in a single-player game the player is supposed to be the protagonist. Never slow the allies.
before.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

after.label: 21. Is the human actually in the score?

before.text:
Rule 6's new 6m range agrees with the wave (the wave only happens within 6m), so on paper the teacher and the legal target are the same thing. before.text:
Item 5 ("asks for another match") is the verdict the whole session hangs on, and Creative's porch screen puts two equal buttons in front of a first-timer who has just lost. People quit to be polite, or because "Finish snow day" reads as the session ending rather than a choice.

before.label: Pass/fail — are the decisions real (hit math + bench arithmetic)
before.text:
Time to clear a ring = reaction (0.60/0.50/0.45s) + 0.25s to step 0.8m + 0.1s slop = 0.95 / 0.85 / 0.80s.
A free, aware, facing kid at 6-10m is hit >=60% (ball 0.65-0.85s). Under 50% = flight time is wrong, not the bots.
Carrier or builder: ~100%. Thrown from outside the ~120° front arc: ~100%.
Overall match hit rate 30-45%. Above 60% the bots are blind; below 25% the hill has no flanking route: fix geometry, not accuracy.
CHILLS: each team 6-12 per round, and no single kid more than 3. That cap is arithmetic, not taste: 3 x 8s = 24s = 13% of a round, which is the only way QA's under-15% bench target can hold. A 4th chill on the same kid is 18% and means that beginner spent the round walking, so it's a geometry or spawn report, not a bench tweak.
Readable miss: >=80% of misses pass within 1.2m of the kid — a maximum gap, measured in Art's projected view, not a screen-space circle. A ball through a body is a collision bug.
Scale: 1280px / 26m ≈ 49px/m. The capture overrides this arithmetic.

before.title: Decided (Foreman)
before.text:
- 1 human + 3 AI allies (Pip, Scoop, Waffle) vs 4 AI. Match = first to 2 rounds (180s each): your hill, their hill, the park only at 1-1 (the decider, rare on purpose).
- Win a round: most crown-seconds with the toboggan. Round 1 sled starts beside the human; rounds 2–3 at the foot, centre. Crown = same flat 4m saddle on every hill. Tie → sudden death, capped 60s.
- Clock: every round runs afternoon → dusk (≥4 steps) → streetlights at 180s, plus a 20s countdown. Lighting resets during the round-result transition, never visibly mid-play.
- Camera: one fixed iso shot, whole ~26m hill on screen, kids ~48px at 720p. No pan. One porch spawn per team.
- No elimination: chilled kid warms up at a cocoa stand at the side of the hill, ~8s total, out of play while there. Target ≤3 chills per kid per round (a test target, not immunity).
- Garage draft (human only) before each round after the first while the match is open: pick 1 of 2, hold one card (shown as a small junk tile on the score strip). Round 1 is always plain snowballs.
- Plain snowball = fast flat line, never clears a wall. Cards: ice chunk (breaks walls), leaf blower (slow lob over walls), snow shovel (instant wall, 3s replant). Everyone has the wall key: one wall, 1s plant at your feet, 8s cooldown shown as a ghost footprint filling at your feet.
- Hits: first kid touched below head height in flight, or anyone in the ring at touchdown. One hit chills. No friendly fire. Hit/miss/splat readable as aftermath.
- AI: Beanie, Pockets (blower), Brick, Copycat; fair-bot rule. Difficulty = reaction 0.45–0.60s + team mix. Allies run Beanie/Pockets/Brick logic.
- Session: up to 3 named streets (Maple Court, Ivy Terrace, The Summit Kids), nothing carries over.
- Controls: move, aim/throw, wall. Throw doubles as sled handoff (carry-capable allies wave for it).

Run: bot CSV (pacing + human-stand-in carry share) → Art's three 1s clips + QA #15's 60s aftermath clip → 3-first-timer session. 2) cards (+ held-card tile). 3) art.

author: claude
summary: edited section “What a good throw feels like (Creative)”

before.title: What a good throw feels like (Creative)
before.text: A snowball is a hard flat line (0.35s + 0.05s/m) that arrives just as the kid flinches. A free, watching kid at 6–10m gets hit ≥60% of the time — reflex-dodging is NOT the skill. 1) The skill is the angle: a kid facing you sees it; a kid at your side, from behind, or busy carrying/building cannot. Match-wide 30–45% hit rate is healthy because most throws come from bad angles. 2) A plain ball NEVER clears a wall — walls are the reason to move. The leaf blower (0.50s + 0.12s/m) is the only slow, walk-out-of-it arc. 3) Protect this: a miss must look like a near miss — ball skidding past the boots, never through them; ≥80% of misses pass within 1.2m.

after.title: What a good throw feels like (Creative)
after.text:
A snowball is a hard flat line (0.35s + 0.05s/m) arriving just as the kid flinches; a free, watching kid at 6–10m is hit ≥60%. Reflex-dodging is NOT the skill.
1) The skill is the angle: a kid facing you sees it; one at your side, behind, or busy carrying/building can't. A 30–45% match hit rate is healthy because most throws come from bad angles.
2) A plain ball NEVER clears a wall — walls are the reason to move. The blower (0.50s + 0.12s/m) is the only slow, walk-out-of-it arc.
3) A miss must look like a near miss: skidding past the boots, never through them; ≥80% of misses within 1.2m.

author: claude
summary: edited section “Greybox verdict rules (QA) — decide bef…”

before.title: Greybox verdict rules (QA) — decide before we look
before.text:
Three first-timers, no coaching, one greybox match: first to 2 rounds, every round on hill A, no cards or draft (phase 1), final camera, ending in place (dusk steps, lights on, 20s countdown).

Watched during the match, nothing asked: 1) touches the sled within 20s of the whistle; 2) hands off (rule 6) before minute 5; 3) presses the wall key unprompted in round 1, and whether a dead second press makes them stop building; 4) says out loud who is winning at 60s and at 150s; 5) asks for another match. Write down their first unprompted complaint, verbatim, with the minute.

Stopwatch, per round: seconds the human cannot act — chilled, walking to the stand, waiting there. Carrying the sled is not downtime, it is play. Target under 15% of a round; over 25% means the bench is too long (5s warm-up) or the stand is too far, not that the tester is bad.

From the same CSV, free: human's share of their team's crown-seconds (want ≥1/3, QA #21) and rounds that reach sudden death (more than 1 in 6 = scoring too flat, QA #21).

Asked only after the match: "what told you time was running out?" (sky vs countdown), "how did you know the sled changed hands?", "did you ever lose sight of the sled or your kid?", "what did you do that changed the score?", "what was the best moment?", "what were you trying to do when you weren't carrying?"

One decision per failure, agreed now:
- never touches the sled → cut a rule or move a spawn, never add a prompt.
- never hands off → fix the ally wave, don't explain it with text.
- never builds → cut the human's wall key and the shovel card; Brick keeps his walls.
- builds once, then stops after a dead second press → the cooldown has no state on screen; add the ghost footprint, no text.
- can't say who's winning → the score strip is wrong, not the tester.
- lost the sled on screen → the fixed camera or the pennant has failed; no new HUD layer.
- wins without ever carrying (share < 1/3) → the allies are the protagonist, not the human: they hold the free sled and wave. No new control.
- shrugs at another match → don't cut the clock yet: read POSSESSION CHANGES in 30s buckets (CSV). Most of them before 90s = the round has no middle, 180 → 120. Still coming near the lights = the ending failed, length wasn't the problem.

AUDIO: temp audio on (whistle, footstep crunch, sled grab/drop shout, ball release, impact, wall break, lights clunk). No sound when a landing ring appears. A capture with no temp audio voids the session.

n=3 proves confusion, not fun. Fun verdict = the host playing a whole match.

entries.label: Diagnosis (from greybox/src/sim/ai.ts)
entries.text: Against a human holding the crown, only Pockets attacks: one blower every 8s with a 1.7s flight, easy to walk out of. Beanie waits for a drop (throws only when the sled has been off the crown 5s+). Copycat only throws when the human throws, and a carrier can't throw. Brick never throws. So 3 of the 4 rivals are passive exactly when the human scores.

entries.label: Fix 1: Siege
entries.text: When an enemy carrier is on or within 2m of the crown, every rival bot that isn't carrying or planting throws at the carrier. Beanie's 5s rule and Copycat's never-initiate rule are suspended during a siege; Brick throws while his wall is up.

entries.label: Fix 2: Bracket
entries.text: Siege throws are staggered so their rings land within ~0.3s of each other: one at the lead point, the others ~1.2m either side. Stepping out of one ring steps into another. Still fair: every ring is visible from commitment, and the carrier can break it by handing off or retreating behind a wall.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Fix 3: the difficulty dial
entries.text: Per street: siege throw cooldown 1.2s → 0.9s → 0.7s and bracket 2 rings → 3. Reaction time stays as the bots' own dodging. This replaces 'reaction time' as the main felt difficulty.

before.label: Fix 2: Bracket
before.text: Siege throws are staggered so their rings land within ~0.3s of each other: one at the lead point, the others ~1.2m either side. Stepping out of one ring steps into another. before.author: claude

after.label: Fix 2: Bracket — lead the carrier, don't line up beside them
after.text:
One volley = N rings released on the same frame (N = 2 on street 1, 3 from street 2; never more than the number of free defenders).

LEAD RING: centre = carrier position + carrier velocity × that throw's own flight time. It lands where the carrier IS GOING, so walking on, or standing still on the crown, is what gets you hit.
OUTER RINGS: same lead, offset ±1.2m perpendicular to the carrier's velocity (if they're near-still, perpendicular to the line from that thrower).
BLOWER RING: its own long flight (0.5 + 0.12s/m) naturally lands ~1s late, aimed at where a carrier fleeing the plain bracket ends up — the slow lob becomes the capper for running away, which is the only job that justifies its speed.

The escape is a read, not a reflex: the free lane is 2.0m (1.2m offset + 0.8m radius) and a 60% carrier takes 0.74s to clear it while a 6–10m plain ball lands in 0.65–0.85s. So the answers are STOP (drop out of the lead), STRAFE the free side on the release frame, or HAND OFF (rule 6) — the volley already in the air lands where the sled was, empty, and the next one needs a fresh 2s to lead the new carrier. Walling the crown is impossible by rule 8; dodge inside the 4m crown circle and you keep scoring.

All rings visible from release. Nothing lands out of frame; no homing.

before.title: Greybox verdict rules (QA) — decide before we look
before.text:
Three first-timers, no coaching, one greybox match: first to 2 rounds, all on hill A, no cards (phase 1), final camera, full ending (dusk, lights, 20s countdown), porch screen.

Watched, nothing asked: 1) touches the sled within 20s; 2) hands off before minute 5 (count silent presses first, QA #23); 3) presses the wall key unprompted in round 1, and whether a press during cooldown stops them building; 4) says aloud who's winning at 60s and 150s; 5) which porch button they press and how long they hover (QA #24). Write down the first unprompted complaint, verbatim, with the minute.

Stopwatch per round: seconds the human can't act (chilled, walking, at the stand; carrying is play). Target <15%; >25% = bench or walk too long, not a bad tester.

From the CSV: human's share of team crown-seconds (QA #21); rounds reaching sudden death (>1 in 6 = scoring too flat).

After the match only: what told you time was running out (sky vs countdown), asked per round? How did you know the sled changed hands? Did you lose sight of the sled or your kid? What did you do that changed the score? Best moment? What were you trying to do when not carrying?

One decision per failure, agreed now:
- never touches the sled → cut a rule or move a spawn, never add a prompt.
- never hands off → fix the ally wave, no text.
- never builds → cut the human's wall key and the shovel; Brick keeps his walls.
- stops building after a press during cooldown → the ghost footprint isn't reading: make it bolder, no text.
- can't say who's winning → the score strip is wrong.
- loses the sled on screen → camera or pennant failed; no new HUD layer.
- human isn't in the score (QA #21 test) → move the round 2–3 sled start toward Chestnut; never slow the allies.
- picks 'Finish snow day' (read with QA #24's hover times) → don't cut the clock yet: read possession changes in 30s buckets. Mostly before 90s = no middle, 180 → 120s. Still coming near the lights = the ending failed, not the length.

AUDIO: temp audio on (whistle, footstep crunch, sled grab/drop shout, ball release, impact, wall break, lights clunk); no sound for a landing ring. No temp audio = void session.

n=3 proves confusion, not fun. Fun verdict = the host playing a whole match.

summary: edited section “Decided (Foreman; host's calls outrank…”

before.title: Decided (Foreman)
before.text:
- 1 human + 3 AI allies (Pip, Scoop, Waffle) vs 4 AI. Match = first to 2 rounds of 180s: your hill, their hill, the park only at 1-1 (rare on purpose).
- Round: most crown-seconds with the toboggan. Sled starts beside the human in round 1, foot-centre in rounds 2–3. Every crown = same flat 4m saddle. Tie → sudden death, capped 60s.
- Clock: afternoon → dusk (≥4 steps) → streetlights at 180s, plus a 20s countdown. Lighting resets in the round-result transition, never mid-play.
- Camera: one fixed iso shot, whole ~26m hill, kids ~48px at 720p. No pan. One porch spawn per team.
- No elimination: a chilled kid warms up at the cocoa stand (side of the hill), ~8s, out of play. Target ≤3 chills per kid per round (a test target, not immunity).
- Garage draft (human only) before rounds 2–3 while the match is open: pick 1 of 2, hold one (junk tile on the score strip). Round 1 = plain snowballs.
- Plain snowball = fast flat line, never clears a wall. Cards: ice chunk (breaks walls), leaf blower (slow lob over walls), snow shovel (instant wall, 3s replant). Everyone's wall key: one wall, 1s plant at your feet, 8s cooldown shown as a filling ghost footprint.
- Hits: first kid touched below head height in flight, or anyone in the ring at touchdown. One hit chills. No friendly fire. Hit/miss/splat read as aftermath.
- AI: Beanie, Pockets (blower), Brick, Copycat; fair-bot rule. Difficulty = reaction 0.45–0.60s + team mix. Allies use Beanie/Pockets/Brick logic.
- Session: up to 3 named streets (Maple Court, Ivy Terrace, The Summit Kids), nothing carries over.
- Controls: move, aim/throw, wall. Throw doubles as sled handoff.

RULESET FROZEN (v4). Changes come only from greybox data or the human session.
BUILD ORDER: 1) Greybox hill A: untextured, per-round dusk + streetlights + 20s countdown, porch screen ('Next street' / 'Finish snow day'), wall ghost, temp audio; 8 bots, plain snowballs + Pockets' blower + ring + first-contact hits + wall, placeholder silhouettes, final camera. Plus static blockouts of the away hill and park (no bots) for Art's 1s flank check before art locks. Run: bot CSV (pacing + stand-in carry share) → Art's three 1s clips + QA #15's 60s clip → 3-first-timer session. 2) Cards (+ held-card tile). 3) Art.

after.title: Decided (Foreman; host's calls outrank everything)

- Clock: afternoon → dusk (≥4 steps) → streetlights at 120s, plus a 20s countdown. Lighting resets between rounds.
- Camera: one fixed iso shot, whole ~26m hill, kids ~48px at 720p. No pan.
- Controls (host): mouse only. Right-click walks toward the cursor, left-click throws (hands off while carrying), middle-click builds.
- No elimination: a chilled kid warms up at the cocoa stand, ~8s, out of play. Target ≤2 chills per kid per round.
- Garage shop (host): credits from hits, crown time and rounds; every kid buys upgrades between rounds (launcher, ice, rock, melter, snowman); they last the match only. Not yet built: bazooka, igloo, fort.
- Plain snowball = fast flat line, never clears a wall. Wall: one per kid, 1s plant at your feet, 8s cooldown (ghost footprint). Nothing built on the crown.

before.title: Greybox verdict rules (QA) — decide before we look
before.text:
Three first-timers, no coaching, one greybox match: first to 2 rounds of 120s, all on hill A, no cards (phase 1), final camera, full ending (dusk, lights, 20s countdown), porch screen.

Watched, nothing asked: 1) touches the sled within 20s; 2) hands off before the first minute (count silent presses first, QA #23); 3) presses the wall key unprompted in round 1, and whether a press during cooldown stops them building; 4) says aloud who's winning at 35s and at 105s; 5) which porch button they press and how long they hover (QA #24); 6) what they look at while carrying (QA #25). Write down the first unprompted complaint, verbatim, with the minute.

Stopwatch per round: seconds the human can't act (chilled, walking, at the stand; carrying is play). Target <15%; >25% = bench or walk too long, not a bad tester.

From the CSV: human's share of team crown-seconds (QA #21); rounds reaching sudden death (>1 in 6 = scoring too flat); crown-hold chills counted separately from open-field chills.

After the match only: what told you time was running out (sky vs countdown), asked per round? How did you know the sled changed hands? Did you lose sight of the sled or your kid? What did you do that changed the score? Best moment? What were you trying to do when not carrying?

One decision per failure, agreed now:
- never touches the sled → cut a rule or move a spawn, never add a prompt.
- never hands off → fix the ally wave, no text.
- never builds → cut the human's wall key and the shovel; Brick keeps his walls.
- stops building after a press during cooldown → the ghost footprint isn't reading: make it bolder, no text.
- can't say who's winning → the score strip is wrong.
- loses the sled on screen → camera or pennant failed; no new HUD layer.
- human isn't in the score (QA #21 test) → move the round 2–3 sled start toward Chestnut; never slow the allies.
- picks 'Finish snow day' (read with QA #24's hover times) → don't cut the clock again, 120s is already short. Read possession changes in 30s buckets: mostly in the first 60s = no middle, fix the crown or geometry; still coming near the lights = the ending failed, not the length.

AUDIO: temp audio on (whistle, footstep crunch, sled grab/drop shout, ball release, impact, wall break, lights clunk); no sound for a landing ring. No temp audio = void session.

n=3 proves confusion, not fun. Fun verdict = the host playing a whole match.

before.label: Fix 3: the difficulty dial is volley cadence, one number
before.text:
Per street: volley period 2.0s → 1.5s → 1.2s, ring count 2 → 3. Reaction time only governs the rivals' own dodging.
CADENCE FLOOR (Foreman, answers QA's trap): a new volley is never released until 0.6s after the previous volley's last ring lands. So stopping on the release frame always buys at least 0.6s plus the next flight to get moving again, whatever the street.
Retune order, one lever at a time: cadence, then lateral spacing (1.2m), then ring count. NEVER shrink the 0.8m ring radius.
before.author: claude

after.label: Fix 3: cadence — the real floor is 1.45s, and the ramp is cappers
after.text:
VOLVOY CADENCE, honest arithmetic. Foreman's floor (0.6s after the last ring lands) must count the PLAIN rings only; the blower capper is allowed to still be airborne when the next volley releases. Otherwise the capper's 1.7s flight gates every volley and all three streets run at ~2.3s — street 1 and street 3 would be identical and the dial would silently do nothing.

True minimum cadence = plain flight to 10m (0.85s) + 0.6s floor = 1.45s. So: 2.0 / 1.5 / 1.45. The approved 1.2s is unreachable — do not ship a value below 1.45.

Therefore the street-3 ramp is NOT cadence: it is capper count and rings. Street 3's mix has two Pockets, so two blowers cap BOTH escape sides instead of one, and the third ring closes the bracket. 2.0s → 1.5s → 1.45s is the cadence part; the rest of the ramp is the blower count.

Retune order, one lever: capper count → ring count → cadence (inside 1.45–2.0) → lateral spacing (1.2m). NEVER shrink the 0.8m ring radius.
after.author: claude
