after.author: claude
after.title: Host playtest 1: the crown is too safe (Systems, implement)

before.label: Fix 2: Bracket — lead the carrier, don't line up beside them
before.text:
One volley = N rings released on the same frame (N = 2 on street 1, 3 from street 2; never more than the number of free defenders).

LEAD RING: centre = carrier position + carrier velocity × that throw's own flight time. It lands where the carrier IS GOING, so walking on, or standing still on the crown, is what gets you hit.
OUTER RINGS: same lead, offset ±1.2m perpendicular to the carrier's velocity (if they're near-still, perpendicular to the line from that thrower).
BLOWER RING: its own long flight (0.5 + 0.12s/m) naturally lands ~1s late, aimed at where a carrier fleeing the plain bracket ends up — the slow lob becomes the capper for running away, which is the only job that justifies its speed.

The escape is a read, not a reflex: the free lane is 2.0m (1.2m offset + 0.8m radius) and a 60% carrier takes 0.74s to clear it while a 6–10m plain ball lands in 0.65–0.85s. So the answers are STOP (drop out of the lead), STRAFE the free side on the release frame, or HAND OFF (rule 6) — the volley already in the air lands where the sled was, empty, and the next one needs a fresh 2s to lead the new carrier. Walling the crown is impossible by rule 8; dodge inside the 4m crown circle and you keep scoring.

All rings visible from release. Nothing lands out of frame; no homing.
before.author: claude

after.label: Fix 2: Bracket — lead the carrier, and only bracket from range
after.text:
One volley = N rings released on the same frame (street 1: 2 rings; street 2–3: 3), never more than the number of free defenders.

LEAD RING: centre = carrier position + carrier velocity × that throw's flight time. Lands where the carrier IS GOING, so walking on, or standing still, is what gets you hit.
OUTER RINGS: same lead, offset ±1.2m perpendicular to the velocity (near-still carrier: perpendicular to the line from that thrower). Street 1 places the outer ring on ONE side only, so the open side is a 1.0m hop; street 2–3 place both, so it is a 2.0m crossing.
BLOWER CAPPER: its own long flight (0.5 + 0.12s/m) lands ~1s late, aimed at where a carrier fleeing the bracket ends up. The slow lob exists to punish the obvious exit.

NEAR-RANGE EXEMPTION — the arithmetic QA broke: clearing 2.0m takes a carrier 0.74s, and a plain ball from 6m lands in 0.65s. So any defender INSIDE 8m throws one direct shot at the lead point and never joins a bracket. 8m+ brackets. You get shelled from across the hill, not elbowed.

WHAT IS NOT AN ESCAPE: stopping is not the answer alone — a stationary carrier is led exactly. The escapes are: hop the 1.0m open side (0.37s, always possible), cross the full 2.0m out of a both-sides bracket (0.74s, only versus ≥8m throwers), or HAND OFF (rule 6) — the volley already airborne lands where the sled was, empty, and the next one needs a fresh cadence to lead the new carrier. Walling the crown is impossible (rule 8); dodge inside the 4m crown circle and you keep scoring.

All rings visible from release. Nothing lands out of frame; no homing.
after.author: claude

before.label: Gate (don't overcorrect)
before.text:
Existing gates hold (now on 120s rounds, host override): crown occupied 25–60% of the round, longest hold ≤25s, ≥6 possession changes per round.

NEW, the one that says the siege is fair: in the bot log, a WILLING carrier's median crown hold on street 1 is 8–20s, and no carrier is chilled by two volleys in a row more than twice per round. SAMPLE: at least 12 holds across 6 rounds, or the median is one lucky carry.

CADENCE TRAP (QA, must be tested before street 3 ships): the street-1 escape is stop-on-the-release-frame — the ring was computed from your velocity, so a stopped carrier is safe. But when volley B is computed, a carrier still standing from volley A has zero velocity, so B lands exactly on them. At 2.0s cadence there is 1.35s to get moving again; at 1.2s there is 0.35s. Run the SAME dodge on all three cadences: if the only reliable escape becomes a hit at 1.2s, cadence is the wrong dial and the ramp should be ring count and spacing.

If a competent carrier never survives 8s: lengthen the volley period first. If the crown is never held at all, the crown is a kill zone and the fix is geometry (cover just outside the crown, or a 2m no-throw band), not a shorter bracket. If holds run past 20s, the siege isn't biting — shorten cadence before adding a ring.

after.label: 4. Garage shop (host override) + economy guards
after.text:
Between rounds every kid (bots included) spends credits in the garage; upgrades last the match, nothing carries to the next street. Credits: 1 per hit, 1 per 6 crown-seconds, 2 per round played, +2 for a round win. Items: launcher 10, ice 6, rock 8, melter 6, snowman 8. Never mid-match. Round 1 = plain snowballs.

SYSTEMS GUARDS: (1) earnings per round CAPPED at 10 — without the cap a hot round (8 hits + 48 crown-s) pays 18 and buys two items, and QA #26's 'one round, one item' becomes fiction. (2) Rival purchases are part of the street tier: no purchase may add a siege ring, shorten volley cadence or remove a dodge window, or the two difficulty dials compound and street 3 stops being measurable. Gates run with all bots shopped to their tier. (3) Spending never touches scoring — crown-seconds alone decide rounds.

WHERE CREDITS ACTUALLY PAY: a carrier can't throw, so upgrades only earn their keep if you hand off (rule 6) and defend Pip's carry with the launcher or rock. The shop is an escort economy, not a carry buff — and if a first-timer never spends, they probably never handed off either, which is one finding, not two.

after.text:
Fix 1's whole argument is that one shared timer makes the volley a single visible event — per-defender releases are what made the old lone blower a coin flip you couldn't read. Fix 2 then exempts everyone inside 8m and lets each of them throw their own direct shot. That is a second, third and fourth release frame, unaligned with the volley, and each arrives faster (0.65s from 6m) than the volley the player is being taught to read. The carrier's job becomes "watch four separate cues while walking at 2.7 m/s", which is precisely the unreadable state the host complained about, wearing different clothes.

FIX: keep the range exemption (the shot's shape differs), delete the extra frames. Every siege ring — direct or bracketed — leaves on the same shared frame each cadence. One release per 2.0 / 1.5 / 1.45s whether it comes from 6m or 20m.

TEST, free from the CSV: count distinct ring-release frames a carrier had to read per volley. More than one per cadence = readability is back where it started, no matter how good the bracket math is.

after.label: 28. The shop fails a beginner two ways, both before any data
after.text:
1) AFFORDABILITY. Credits: 1 per hit + 1 per 6 crown-seconds + 2 for playing, capped at 10. Cheapest item is 6. A player whose team never held the crown and landed two hits walks into the shop with 4 and can buy nothing. The worse the round, the emptier the reward — a negative spiral aimed exactly at the first-timer we are measuring, and it reads as a broken screen, not as a bad game.

FIX: price the cheapest item at what a bad round pays (4), or pay 4 just for playing. The shop must never be a locked door.

2) IT IS THE ONLY SCREEN WITH NUMBERS. The rule is that the game's only words are two lines on the porch screen. A shop needs credits and prices. Do not add text: credits as a row of pips, each item's price as the same pips beside its junk tile, so the screen is objects and counts.

TEST: after the shop, ask "what could you afford?" If they have to count out loud twice, the pips aren't reading — and the shop is the wrong screen, not the wrong font.

before.text:

after.label: 4. Garage shop + economy guards (prices on a 4/8/10 ladder)
after.text:
Between rounds every kid (bots included) spends credits in the garage; upgrades last the match, nothing carries to the next street. Credits: 1 per hit, 1 per 6 crown-seconds, 4 for playing a round, +2 for a round win. Items: ice 4, melter 4, rock 8, snowman 8, launcher 10. Never mid-match. Round 1 = plain snowballs.

PRICE LADDER — Foreman's +2 to the round-play credit still leaves the first shop empty, because the worst round is 4 credits and the cheapest item was 6. Fix the prices, not the pay: cheapest = 4 = exactly what a round with no hits and no crown pays, so the shelf is never bare (QA #28). Then 8, then 10: one impulse buy, one save-up, one goal.

GUARD, corrected: cap the PURCHASE, not the income — ONE purchase per shop visit. A 10-credit income cap would make a great round pay exactly what a good round pays and flatten the only reward signal a match has; one-purchase-per-visit is the actual QA #26 limit and lets the surplus bank toward next round's 10.

(2) Rival purchases are part of the street tier: no purchase may add a siege ring, shorten volley cadence or remove a dodge window; gates run with all bots shopped to their tier. (3) Spending never touches scoring.

WHERE CREDITS PAY: a carrier can't throw, so upgrades only earn out through rule 6's handoff — hand off and defend Pip's carry with the launcher or rock. The shop is an escort economy; a first-timer who never spends probably never handed off either, which is one finding, not two.

after.title: Host playtest 1: the crown is too safe (Systems, implement)

before.label: Fix 2: Bracket — lead the carrier, and only bracket from range
before.text:
One volley = N rings released on the same frame (street 1: 2 rings; street 2–3: 3), never more than the number of free defenders.

LEAD RING: centre = carrier position + carrier velocity × that throw's flight time. Lands where the carrier IS GOING, so walking on, or standing still, is what gets you hit.
OUTER RINGS: same lead, offset ±1.2m perpendicular to the velocity (near-still carrier: perpendicular to the line from that thrower). Street 1 places the outer ring on ONE side only, so the open side is a 1.0m hop; street 2–3 place both, so it is a 2.0m crossing.
BLOWER CAPPER: its own long flight (0.5 + 0.12s/m) lands ~1s late, aimed at where a carrier fleeing the bracket ends up. The slow lob exists to punish the obvious exit.

NEAR-RANGE EXEMPTION — the arithmetic QA broke: clearing 2.0m takes a carrier 0.74s, and a plain ball from 6m lands in 0.65s. So any defender INSIDE 8m throws one direct shot at the lead point and never joins a bracket. 8m+ brackets. You get shelled from across the hill, not elbowed.

WHAT IS NOT AN ESCAPE: stopping is not the answer alone — a stationary carrier is led exactly. The escapes are: hop the 1.0m open side (0.37s, always possible), cross the full 2.0m out of a both-sides bracket (0.74s, only versus ≥8m throwers), or HAND OFF (rule 6) — the volley already airborne lands where the sled was, empty, and the next one needs a fresh cadence to lead the new carrier. Walling the crown is impossible (rule 8); dodge inside the 4m crown circle and you keep scoring.

All rings visible from release. Nothing lands out of frame; no homing.
before.author: claude

after.label: Fix 2: Bracket — lead from range, no lead up close, one release frame
after.text:
One volley = N rings released on the SAME frame (street 1: 2 rings; street 2–3: 3), never more than the number of free defenders. Rivals inside 8m release on that frame too, with a different shot — the player only ever reads one release (Foreman's ruling).

FAR (8m+, brackets): LEAD RING centre = carrier position + carrier velocity × flight time, so running on is what gets you hit. OUTER RINGS ±1.2m perpendicular to the velocity (near-still carrier: perpendicular to the thrower line). Street 1 puts the outer ring on ONE side (open side = a 1.0m hop); streets 2–3 put both (open side = a 2.0m crossing = 0.74s at carrier speed, only survivable versus ≥8m throwers at 0.75–0.85s flight).

NEAR (under 8m, single direct shot): NO LEAD — aim at the carrier's position at release. At 6m the flight is 0.55s, so a carrier moving at 2.7 m/s is 1.5m away on touchdown and cannot be hit; a carrier who stopped is hit dead centre.

That pairing is the design: the far bracket punishes RUNNING, the near shot punishes STOPPING, the blower capper punishes the obvious exit. Irregular movement is the skill; no single crouch-and-wait or sprint-straight answer survives.

BLOWER CAPPER: its own long flight (0.5 + 0.12s/m) lands ~1s late, aimed at where a carrier fleeing the bracket ends up. HANDOFF stays the free escape: the volley already airborne lands where the sled was, empty. Walling the crown is impossible (rule 8); dodge inside the 4m crown circle and you keep scoring. All rings visible from release, nothing out of frame, no homing.
after.author: claude

after.text:
The capper outlives the cadence: a blower from 14m flies 2.18s (0.5 + 0.12s/m) against street 3's 1.45s volley, so volley B releases while volley A's plain rings and capper are still landing. summary: edited section “What a good throw feels like (Creative)”

before.title: What a good throw feels like (Creative)
before.text:
A snowball is a hard flat line (0.35s + 0.05s/m) arriving just as the kid flinches; a free, watching kid at 6–10m is hit ≥60%. Reflex-dodging is NOT the skill.
1) The skill is the angle: a kid facing you sees it; one at your side, behind, or busy carrying/building can't. A 30–45% match hit rate is healthy because most throws come from bad angles.
2) A plain ball NEVER clears a wall — walls are the reason to move. The blower (0.50s + 0.12s/m) is the only slow, walk-out-of-it arc.
3) A miss must look like a near miss: skidding past the boots, never through them; ≥80% of misses within 1.2m.

before.title: Greybox verdict rules (QA) — decide before we look
before.text:
Three first-timers, no coaching, one greybox match: first to 2 rounds of 120s, all on hill A, final camera, full ending (dusk, lights, 20s countdown), porch screen.

Watched, nothing asked: 1) touches the sled within 20s; 2) hands off before the first minute (count silent presses first, QA #23); 3) presses the build button unprompted in round 1, and whether a press during cooldown stops them building; 4) says aloud who's winning at 35s and at 105s; 5) which porch button they press and how long they hover (QA #24); 6) what they look at while carrying (QA #25). Write down the first unprompted complaint, verbatim, with the minute.

Stopwatch per round: seconds the human can't act (chilled, walking, at the stand; carrying is play). Target <15%; >25% = bench or walk too long, not a bad tester.

From the CSV: human's share of team crown-seconds (QA #21); rounds reaching sudden death (>1 in 6 = scoring too flat); crown-hold chills counted separately from open-field chills.

After the match only: what told you time was running out (sky vs countdown), asked per round? How did you know the sled changed hands? Did you lose sight of the sled or your kid? What did you do that changed the score? Best moment? What were you trying to do when not carrying? Did you reopen the shop on purpose?

One decision per failure, agreed now:
- never touches the sled → cut a rule or move a spawn, never add a prompt.
- never hands off → fix the ally wave, no text.
- never builds → cut the human's build button; Brick keeps his walls.
- stops building after a press during cooldown → the ghost footprint isn't reading: make it bolder, no text.
- can't say who's winning → the score strip is wrong.
- loses the sled on screen → camera or pennant failed; no new HUD layer.
- human isn't in the score (QA #21 test) → move the round 2–3 sled start toward Chestnut; never slow the allies.
- picks 'Finish snow day' (read with QA #24's hover times) → don't cut the clock again, 120s is already short. Read possession changes in 30s buckets: mostly in the first 60s = no middle, fix the crown or geometry; still coming near the lights = the ending failed, not the length.

AUDIO: temp audio on (whistle, footstep crunch, sled grab/drop shout, ball release, impact, wall break, lights clunk); no sound for a landing ring. No temp audio = void session.

n=3 proves confusion, not fun. Fun verdict = the host playing a whole match.

author: claude
summary: edited “4. Garage shop + economy (4/8/10 price…” in Core loop rules — Systems (implement exactly)

before.label: 4. Garage shop + economy guards (prices on a 4/8/10 ladder)
before.text:
Between rounds every kid (bots included) spends credits in the garage; upgrades last the match, nothing carries to the next street. Credits: 1 per hit, 1 per 6 crown-seconds, 4 for playing a round, +2 for a round win. Items: ice 4, melter 4, rock 8, snowman 8, launcher 10. Never mid-match. Round 1 = plain snowballs.

PRICE LADDER — Foreman's +2 to the round-play credit still leaves the first shop empty, because the worst round is 4 credits and the cheapest item was 6. Fix the prices, not the pay: cheapest = 4 = exactly what a round with no hits and no crown pays, so the shelf is never bare (QA #28). Then 8, then 10: one impulse buy, one save-up, one goal.

GUARD, corrected: cap the PURCHASE, not the income — ONE purchase per shop visit. A 10-credit income cap would make a great round pay exactly what a good round pays and flatten the only reward signal a match has; one-purchase-per-visit is the actual QA #26 limit and lets the surplus bank toward next round's 10.

(2) Rival purchases are part of the street tier: no purchase may add a siege ring, shorten volley cadence or remove a dodge window; gates run with all bots shopped to their tier. (3) Spending never touches scoring.

WHERE CREDITS PAY: a carrier can't throw, so upgrades only earn out through rule 6's handoff — hand off and defend Pip's carry with the launcher or rock. The shop is an escort economy; a first-timer who never spends probably never handed off either, which is one finding, not two.

after.label: 4. Garage shop + economy (4/8/10 price ladder)
after.text:

PRICES: ice 4, melter 4, rock 8, snowman 8, launcher 10. Cheapest = 4 = a no-hit, no-crown round, so the shelf is never bare (QA #28). One impulse buy, one save-up, one goal.
GUARDS: ONE purchase per visit — cap purchases, not income, so a great round banks toward 10. Rival purchases stay inside the street tier (no extra siege ring, shorter cadence or lost dodge window). Spending never touches scoring.

summary: edited “13. Busy vs free stance” in Core loop rules — Systems (implement exactly)

before.label: 13. The one stance that matters (dodge vs walk)
before.text: Two states, one information: BUSY (sled hugged in both arms, or bent over planting) and FREE. A busy kid cannot LEAN-DODGE — the 0.25s sidestep that clears a 0.8m ring without giving up their line. They can still WALK at 60%, which is all a carrier has: 2.7 m/s, so 1.0m out of a ring in 0.37s and 2.0m in 0.74s. That gap is exactly why the siege bites and why the bracket has to come from range. Free kids can lean-dodge. The pose is the information; the rest is identity.

before.label: 27. One release frame per cadence — RULED (Foreman): close defenders keep their direct shot but release on the volley frame
before.text:
Fix 1's whole argument is that one shared timer makes the volley a single visible event — per-defender releases are what made the old lone blower a coin flip you couldn't read. Fix 2 then exempts everyone inside 8m and lets each of them throw their own direct shot. That is a second, third and fourth release frame, unaligned with the volley, and each arrives faster (0.65s from 6m) than the volley the player is being taught to read. The carrier's job becomes "watch four separate cues while walking at 2.7 m/s", which is precisely the unreadable state the host complained about, wearing different clothes.

FIX: keep the range exemption (the shot's shape differs), delete the extra frames. Every siege ring — direct or bracketed — leaves on the same shared frame each cadence. One release per 2.0 / 1.5 / 1.45s whether it comes from 6m or 20m.

TEST, free from the CSV: count distinct ring-release frames a carrier had to read per volley. More than one per cadence = readability is back where it started, no matter how good the bracket math is.

before.label: 28. Shop beginner problem — RULED: 4 credits per round played; text allowed on the shop screen
before.text:
1) AFFORDABILITY. Credits: 1 per hit + 1 per 6 crown-seconds + 2 for playing, capped at 10. Cheapest item is 6. A player whose team never held the crown and landed two hits walks into the shop with 4 and can buy nothing. The worse the round, the emptier the reward — a negative spiral aimed exactly at the first-timer we are measuring, and it reads as a broken screen, not as a bad game.

FIX: price the cheapest item at what a bad round pays (4), or pay 4 just for playing. The shop must never be a locked door.

2) IT IS THE ONLY SCREEN WITH NUMBERS. The rule is that the game's only words are two lines on the porch screen. A shop needs credits and prices. Do not add text: credits as a row of pips, each item's price as the same pips beside its junk tile, so the screen is objects and counts.

TEST: after the shop, ask "what could you afford?" If they have to count out loud twice, the pips aren't reading — and the shop is the wrong screen, not the wrong font.

before.label: 29. Live rings at once — the real difficulty dial, and street 2–3 may fail it
before.text:
The capper outlives the cadence: a blower from 14m flies 2.18s (0.5 + 0.12s/m) against street 3's 1.45s volley, so volley B releases while volley A's plain rings and capper are still landing. Street 3 runs two Pockets, so that is up to ~6 rings live in front of one carrier, at 48px, on dusk snow. Nothing measures this: the hold-median gate can be passed by luck.

FREE FROM THE CSV: at each release frame, count rings already released and not yet landed. Report the MAX LIVE RINGS any one carrier faced, per round.
RED LINE: more than 4 (one bracket of 3 + one capper) is a readability fail no matter how good the hold times look.
IF IT FAILS: cadence stops being the ramp. Hold 2.0s on all three streets and ramp ring count (2→3) and capper count (1→2) instead — 2.0s also retires the 1.45s floor whoever computes it next has to keep re-deriving.

Do not change it before the log exists; this is a measurement to add now, a lever to pull after.

after.label: 29. Max live rings — the real difficulty dial
after.text: A 14m blower flies 2.18s against street 3's 1.45s cadence, so volleys overlap: up to ~6 live rings on one carrier at dusk, and the hold median can pass by luck. before.label: 31. The siege and the 15% stopwatch rule out the same round
before.text:
A chill costs ~8s (walk, warm, jog back) out of 120s, so the agreed 'human can't act <15%' target allows the human exactly TWO chills per round. Three is 20% and fails.

The gates contradict each other at the top of their own ranges: a willing carrier holding 20s, over two or three carries, is chilled at the end of most holds — three chills, gate blown — while the crown is behaving perfectly. Crown chills are counted separately from open-field chills, so nothing fires.

FIX AT REPORT TIME: report human chills and human bench-second total as ONE number, not split by where the ball came from. If bench >15% while holds sit inside 8–20s, the punishment is too long, not the crown: 8s warm-up → 5s is the first lever, moving the stand the second. Never shorten cadence to fix a bench number.

before.label: Behaviour rules (Systems) — no state trees
before.text:
Beanie: grabs a free sled or one whose carrier is chilled, shortest legal path to the crown. Throws only when the sled has been off the crown 5s+. Never builds.
Pockets: leaf blower. Holds 6–10m from the nearest enemy, faces the enemy carrier, backs off inside 6m. Carries only as fallback.
Brick: never carries, receives or throws. Keeps his one wall between his carrier and the nearest threat, outside the crown and ≥2m from the sled. Wall down: walks 2m ahead of the carrier as a shield.
Copycat: 2s after the human acts, repeats that action type; never initiates. In bot runs copies the stand-in.
SIEGE (both teams): an enemy carrying the sled within 2m of the crown puts the team on a shared 2.0s volley that suspends Beanie's 5s rule and Copycat's never-initiate rule. See 'Host playtest 1' for the bracket. Brick still never throws.
FAIR-BOT: react only to COMMITTED rings in the ~120° facing arc, at human move speed (4.5 m/s). Carriers and builders don't dodge.
Difficulty = siege cadence (2.0/1.5/1.2s) + team mix (rule 10); reaction 0.45–0.60s only governs their dodging. Fallback carrier when Beanie is chilled 3s+: Pockets, then Copycat.
ALLIES: Beanie, Pockets, Brick logic; never take the sled from the human.
HUMAN STAND-IN (bot runs): Beanie logic, plain snowballs; in the cards phase holds the card under test.

before.label: Fix 1: Siege — one shared volley, not per-bot cadences
before.text:
TRIGGER: an enemy kid carries the sled within 2m of the crown edge. From that frame the defending team is in SIEGE until the sled is dropped, free, carried away from the crown by 2m+, or is carried by the defending team.

During siege every defender that is not chilled, carrying or mid-plant joins ONE shared volley timer (2.0s on street 1). One timer, so all rings are a single visible event — per-bot cooldowns are what made the old blower dodgeable alone. Siege suspends Beanie's 5s rule and Copycat's never-initiate rule for volley throws only.

before.label: Fix 2: Bracket — lead from range, no lead up close, one release frame
before.text:
One volley = N rings released on the SAME frame (street 1: 2 rings; street 2–3: 3), never more than the number of free defenders. Rivals inside 8m release on that frame too, with a different shot — the player only ever reads one release (Foreman's ruling).

FAR (8m+, brackets): LEAD RING centre = carrier position + carrier velocity × flight time, so running on is what gets you hit. OUTER RINGS ±1.2m perpendicular to the velocity (near-still carrier: perpendicular to the thrower line). Street 1 puts the outer ring on ONE side (open side = a 1.0m hop); streets 2–3 put both (open side = a 2.0m crossing = 0.74s at carrier speed, only survivable versus ≥8m throwers at 0.75–0.85s flight).

NEAR (under 8m, single direct shot): NO LEAD — aim at the carrier's position at release. At 6m the flight is 0.55s, so a carrier moving at 2.7 m/s is 1.5m away on touchdown and cannot be hit; a carrier who stopped is hit dead centre.

That pairing is the design: the far bracket punishes RUNNING, the near shot punishes STOPPING, the blower capper punishes the obvious exit. Irregular movement is the skill; no single crouch-and-wait or sprint-straight answer survives.

BLOWER CAPPER: its own long flight (0.5 + 0.12s/m) lands ~1s late, aimed at where a carrier fleeing the bracket ends up. HANDOFF stays the free escape: the volley already airborne lands where the sled was, empty. Walling the crown is impossible (rule 8); dodge inside the 4m crown circle and you keep scoring. All rings visible from release, nothing out of frame, no homing.
before.author: claude

after.label: Fix 2: Bracket — lead from range, none up close, one release frame
after.text:
One volley = N rings on the SAME frame (street 1: 2; streets 2–3: 3), never more than free defenders.
FAR (8m+): lead ring = carrier position + velocity × flight time; outer rings ±1.2m perpendicular to velocity. Street 1: outer ring one side (escape = 1.0m hop); streets 2–3: both (2.0m = 0.74s at carrier speed).
NEAR (<8m): one direct shot at the carrier's position, no lead, same frame. A moving carrier is 1.5m away on touchdown; a stopped one is hit.
The bracket punishes running, the near shot punishes stopping, the blower capper (lands ~1s late) punishes the obvious exit. Irregular movement is the skill.
Handoff is the free escape: the volley lands where the sled was. Dodging inside the 4m crown keeps scoring. All rings visible from release, no homing.

before.text:
VOLVOY CADENCE, honest arithmetic. Foreman's floor (0.6s after the last ring lands) must count the PLAIN rings only; the blower capper is allowed to still be airborne when the next volley releases. Otherwise the capper's 1.7s flight gates every volley and all three streets run at ~2.3s — street 1 and street 3 would be identical and the dial would silently do nothing.

True minimum cadence = plain flight to 10m (0.85s) + 0.6s floor = 1.45s. So: 2.0 / 1.5 / 1.45. The approved 1.2s is unreachable — do not ship a value below 1.45.

Therefore the street-3 ramp is NOT cadence: it is capper count and rings. Street 3's mix has two Pockets, so two blowers cap BOTH escape sides instead of one, and the third ring closes the bracket. 2.0s → 1.5s → 1.45s is the cadence part; the rest of the ramp is the blower count.

Retune order, one lever: capper count → ring count → cadence (inside 1.45–2.0) → lateral spacing (1.2m). NEVER shrink the 0.8m ring radius.
before.author: claude

after.label: Fix 3: cadence floor 1.45s; the ramp is cappers
after.text:
The 0.6s floor counts plain rings only; a blower capper may still be airborne at the next release, or every street collapses to ~2.3s. Floor = 0.85s + 0.6s = 1.45s (rule 10). The street-3 ramp is capper count, not cadence.
Retune one lever at a time: capper count → ring count → cadence (1.45–2.0s) → lateral spacing (1.2m). Never shrink the 0.8m ring.
after.author: claude

before.label: Gate (don't overcorrect)
before.text:
Existing gates hold (120s rounds): crown occupied 25–60% of the round, longest hold ≤25s, ≥6 possession changes per round.

NEW, the one that says the siege is fair: in the bot log, a WILLING carrier's median crown hold on street 1 is 8–20s, and no carrier is chilled by two volleys in a row more than twice per round. SAMPLE: at least 12 holds across 6 rounds, or the median is one lucky carry.

NEAR-RANGE CHECK, free from the CSV: log thrower distance on every siege ring. If most crown chills come from inside 8m, the near-range exemption isn't implemented and the crown is a mugging, not artillery.

If a competent carrier never survives 8s: lengthen the volley period first. If the crown is never held at all, it's a kill zone — fix geometry (cover just outside the crown, or a 2m no-throw band), not the bracket. If holds run past 20s, add a capper before shortening cadence.

before.title: Decided (Foreman; host's calls outrank everything)
before.text:
- 1 human + 3 AI allies (Pip, Scoop, Waffle) vs 4 AI. Match = first to 2 rounds of 120s (host): your hill, their hill, the park only at 1-1.
- Round: most crown-seconds with the toboggan. Sled starts beside the human in round 1, foot-centre in rounds 2–3. Every crown = same flat saddle. Tie → sudden death, capped 60s.
- Clock: afternoon → dusk (≥4 steps) → streetlights at 120s, plus a 20s countdown. Lighting resets between rounds.
- Camera: one fixed iso shot, whole ~26m hill, kids ~48px at 720p. No pan.
- Controls (host): mouse only. Right-click walks toward the cursor, left-click throws (hands off while carrying), middle-click builds.
- No elimination: a chilled kid warms up at the cocoa stand, ~8s, out of play. Target ≤2 chills per kid per round.
- Garage shop (host): credits from hits, crown time and rounds (4 per round guaranteed, cap 10); every kid buys upgrades between rounds (launcher, ice, rock, melter, snowman); they last the match only. Shop screen may use text. Not yet built: bazooka, igloo, fort.
- Plain snowball = fast flat line, never clears a wall. Wall: one per kid, 1s plant at your feet, 8s cooldown (ghost footprint). Nothing built on the crown.
- Hits: first kid touched below head height in flight, or anyone in the ring at touchdown. One hit chills. No friendly fire.
- AI: Beanie, Pockets (blower), Brick (never throws), Copycat; fair-bot dodging.
- SIEGE: whoever holds the crown faces one shared volley, ONE release frame per cadence. Defenders 8m+ bracket the carrier's path; closer ones throw one direct shot on the same frame. Cadence 2.0 / 1.5 / 1.45s per street; street 3 adds a second blower (two Pockets).
- Session: up to 3 named streets (Maple Court, Ivy Terrace, The Summit Kids); nothing carries between streets.

NEXT: Systems builds the siege, reruns the bot log against the 'Host playtest 1' limits, then the host plays again.

before.label: Fix 2: Bracket — lead from range, none up close, one release frame
before.text:
One volley = N rings on the SAME frame (street 1: 2; streets 2–3: 3), never more than free defenders.
FAR (8m+): lead ring = carrier position + velocity × flight time; outer rings ±1.2m perpendicular to velocity. Street 1: outer ring one side (escape = 1.0m hop); streets 2–3: both (2.0m = 0.74s at carrier speed).
NEAR (<8m): one direct shot at the carrier's position, no lead, same frame. A moving carrier is 1.5m away on touchdown; a stopped one is hit.
The bracket punishes running, the near shot punishes stopping, the blower capper (lands ~1s late) punishes the obvious exit. Irregular movement is the skill.
Handoff is the free escape: the volley lands where the sled was. Dodging inside the 4m crown keeps scoring. All rings visible from release, no homing.

before.label: Behaviour rules (Systems) — no state trees

Pockets: blower; holds 6–10m from the nearest enemy, faces their carrier, backs off inside 6m. Carries only as fallback.
Brick: never carries, receives or throws. Keeps his wall between his carrier and the nearest threat (outside the crown, ≥2m from the sled); wall down = walks 2m ahead as a shield.
Copycat: 2s after the human acts, repeats that action type; never initiates (copies the stand-in in bot runs).
SIEGE suspends Beanie's 5s rule and Copycat's never-initiate rule (Host playtest 1).
FAIR-BOT: reacts only to committed rings in its ~120° front arc, at 4.5 m/s. Carriers and builders don't dodge.
Difficulty = siege cadence + team mix (rule 10); reaction 0.45–0.60s governs dodging only. Fallback carrier when Beanie is chilled 3s+: Pockets, then Copycat.
ALLIES: same logic; never take the sled from the human.
STAND-IN (bot runs): Beanie logic, plain snowballs; in shop tests buys the item under test.

entries.text: After a match the streetlights are on and Frosty wakes up on the crown. Your kid alone versus Frosty, 45s, same hill. Frosty is a giant snowman: 3 hits to melt (the snowman rule) and he can't move. He attacks with the siege volley (a bracket aimed at where you're walking, plus a lob), so no new attack system is needed. Hit him 3 times before the 45s is up and you win. The 1v1 kid duel adds nothing the main game doesn't already have.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Escalation in one number
entries.text: Frosty uses the street's own siege row (rule 10): street 1 is gentle, street 3 throws a lob at both exits. Optional twist: each hit makes him angrier and shortens his volley timing by one step.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Prize: one free garage item for the next street
entries.text: Worth the cheapest tier (4 credits), and only for the next street; a new snow day still starts clean. It's small and you feel it straight away. Alternative: a cosmetic only (Frosty's carrot pinned to your scarf for the rest of the snow day), with no effect on gameplay.

entries.label: Sit it after the porch, never before it
entries.text: The porch's 'Next street' / 'Finish snow day' hover is our only read on whether the ladder is worth continuing (#24). A bout between the streetlights and the porch delays that read and charges the ladder a fight nobody asked for. Cheap fix: 'Next street' plays the bout, then the street's porch; 'Finish snow day' skips it. No third button — and the bout becomes a retention measure: does the player who just lost still want to be here?
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: Prize: not credits, and losing never costs
entries.text:
Credits are the one decision the shop has left: 4/8/10 with one purchase per visit means cheap-now or save for the launcher. A boss payout buys the launcher at street 2 and that choice is gone, and one 30s bout then out-earns a 120s round of play.
Legal prizes, in order: nothing but a porch line; one free garage item at the next shop that expires when that match ends (no carry past it, no lasting unlock).
LOSING THE BOUT MUST NEVER COST ANYTHING. After a lost match that is the worst moment this game could have.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: No cocoa stand in a 1v1
entries.text:
A chill is ~8s at the stand and your allies cover it. In a 1v1 it is a stunlock: Frosty lands one lob, you walk back, he lands another, and the bout is unwinnable however well you read rings — plus it puts the game's only punishment for a beginner on a mode with no team to bail them out.
BOUT RULE: a hit costs tempo (knockback + cancelled throw), or three hits end it on the clock. Never the bench.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: Frosty = the siege with one thrower (the exam)
entries.text:
Do not give him new attacks. One release frame, a bracket that leads you from 8m+, one late capper lob: a solo version of the read a four-kid scrum never taught cleanly, with nothing new to balance. Rings land 2, not 4.
GIVE HIM A SLOW WALK between two spots. A static turret 20m away is a dodge-and-throw chore; moving means his busy pose while lobbing is the hit window rule 13 already defines, and the crouch-and-wait answer dies.
20–30s on a fixed clock. He is a bonus, so no pass/fail gate rides on him — the only thing measured is whether a first-timer can describe what he was about to do.

before.label: 7. Throwing: aim a spot, hard line
before.text:
Mouse aims a landing ring (r 0.8m); left-click throws. Ring visible to all from commitment; ball casts a shadow dot. Your own ring hides while you carry; the handoff outline replaces it (QA #25).

- Ice: 0.25s + 0.03s/m, flat, 12m, shatters the wall it hits.
- Rock: plain flight (0.35s + 0.05s/m, 12m) but smashes through walls and snowmen and keeps going; a kid it chills is knocked 1.5m off the spot, so a carrier lands away from the sled they dropped.

- Snowman: your build button makes a snowman instead of a wall (3 hits to break, 12s cooldown); it pelts rivals within 8m every 2.2s.

Pockets: blower only; holds 6–10m from the nearest enemy, faces their carrier, backs off inside 6m. Carries only as fallback.
Brick: never carries, receives or throws. Keeps his wall between his carrier and the nearest threat (outside the crown, ≥2m from the sled); wall down = walks 2m ahead as a shield.
Copycat: 2s after the human acts, repeats that action type; never initiates (copies the stand-in in bot runs).
SIEGE suspends Beanie's 5s rule and Copycat's never-initiate rule (Host playtest 1).
FAIR-BOT: reacts only to committed rings in its ~120° front arc, after its reaction time, by walking 0.8m out (rule 11). Carriers and builders don't dodge.
Difficulty = street tier (rule 10); reaction 0.45–0.60s governs dodging only. Fallback carrier when Beanie is chilled 3s+: Pockets, then Copycat.
ALLIES: same logic. They never take a handoff the human didn't give, but a sled the human drops is free for anyone, allies included (6b stays ruled out).
SHOPPING: wishlists in rule 4.
STAND-IN (bot runs): Beanie logic, plain snowballs; in shop tests buys the item under test.

summary: added “Hit budget: the clock is not the constr…” to Boss bout: Frosty (merged spec, Foreman + Systems + QA)

after.label: Hit budget: the clock is not the constraint, so tune specials first
after.text:
The arithmetic for 60s / 10 hits, plain ball (0.85s flight at 10m), one throw per 0.6s:
60s − 3 specials × (2.5–4.0s warning + ~1s release + 2s dizzy) ≈ 21s of special, of which ~6s dizzy is free throwing → ~45s of throwing, ~75 throws, 10 needed. Against a static target that never dodges that is a ~13% accuracy requirement: 10 hits is a pacing device, not a skill test. Good — it means a first-timer normally wins, which is why the prize must be cosmetic.
The fail state is therefore entirely the specials and his normal volleys. TUNING ORDER if the bout is too easy or too hard: 1) special frequency (15s → 12/18s), 2) hits to melt (10 → 8/12), 3) fort distance from Frosty. Never the 60s clock and never the 2.5/4.0s warnings — the warnings are the fairness promise, not a difficulty dial.

entries.label: Two specials, two different mistakes (answers Creative's challenge)
entries.text:
If both specials are answered by 'be behind a fort', the second one is a reskin: same input, same result, twice the art. So the pair is split by how you fail:
- BURST (2.5s, radial, no gap) = you were too far from cover when it started. Mistake: out of position.
- BOULDERS (4.0s, three 2.5m lanes) = you stood still in a marked lane, or you were mid-commit and couldn't move (rule 13). Mistake: didn't read the lane / threw at the wrong time.
Both still leave the fort as the safe answer, so the host's instant-loss-unless-sheltered rule is untouched for the burst; the boulder is the one attack where the drawn lane is also a legal answer, which is the only reason it exists.
IF the host wants the boulder shelter-only too: make each lane 6m wide so the three span the hill and there is no strip to stand in. Accept that the two specials are then one attack in two costumes, and expect to cut one after the first playtest.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Hit budget: the clock is not the constraint, so tune specials first
entries.text:
The arithmetic for 60s / 10 hits, plain ball (0.85s flight at 10m), one throw per 0.6s:
60s − 3 specials × (2.5–4.0s warning + ~1s release + 2s dizzy) ≈ 21s of special, of which ~6s dizzy is free throwing → ~45s of throwing, ~75 throws, 10 needed. Against a static target that never dodges that is a ~13% accuracy requirement: 10 hits is a pacing device, not a skill test. Good — it means a first-timer normally wins, which is why the prize must be cosmetic.
The fail state is therefore entirely the specials and his normal volleys. TUNING ORDER if the bout is too easy or too hard: 1) special frequency (15s → 12/18s), 2) hits to melt (10 → 8/12), 3) fort distance from Frosty. Never the 60s clock and never the 2.5/4.0s warnings — the warnings are the fairness promise, not a difficulty dial.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Art fairness gate — shelter is geometry, not a particle count
entries.text: 24 discrete balls do not prove a gapless burst; validate projectile width/spacing at the farthest playable radius. Any collision envelope must match the visible snow, never invisible damage between balls. Freeze warning clips at 720p: first-timer points to safe side of fort, then reaches it with right-click before release from the worst legal position. Include acceleration/path around fort, not just straight-line distance. Host asked both specials to require shelter: sidestep-safe boulders remain an unapproved exception, not a settled rule.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: The warning is longer than the arena — the instant loss can't fire
entries.text:
2.5s at 4.5 m/s buys 11m of running. The forts sit ~7m out on a ~26m hill, so a kid who reads the flakes even once is behind cover every time and the instant loss never happens.

So the special's real job, per the arithmetic, is a TIME TAX: 3 × (2.5s warning + ~1s release + 2s dizzy) ≈ 16.5s, a quarter of a 60s bout spent walking to a rock and back. Survivable, but not a decision.

Don't shorten the warnings — they're the fairness promise. Pick one:
- SPREAD the forts so the safe side is 8m+ from where a good thrower wants to stand: the dash becomes a route, not a twitch; or
- accept the time tax and CUT to one special if the log shows zero instant losses.

FREE FROM THE LOG: per bout, distance to nearest shelter at warning start, seconds to reach it, and whether the special killed. 10 bouts, no deaths = the warning IS the attack.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: The trophy is invisible — nothing on screen shows it
entries.text:
Every version of the prize now ends as Frosty's pot hat "on your porch snowman for the rest of the snow day", but the porch screen is two lines of text and the only snowman object in the game is a bought build item. As written, you win the trophy and never see it again.

CHEAP FIX: a small snowman wearing the pot stands at the foot of YOUR porch, on the field, in every later round of the snow day. Static, low, no pennant, never near the crown — it must never be readable as scoring (history stays off the crown, per the ruled-out pennant). Then "I melted him" is something a kid points at, not a line they read.

entries.label: Frosty: 60s, 10 hits to melt, you can take 3 (host)
entries.text: Your kid alone against Frosty on the same hill, 60s, streetlights on. Frosty sits on the crown, never moves or dodges, and is big and easy to hit. entries.label: Frosty's attacks: normal throws + 2 specials (host)
entries.text:
NORMAL: aimed siege volleys at you (lead ring + direct ring + lob). A hit = one of your 3.
SPECIAL 1, BLIZZARD BURST: a full ring of 24 flat snowballs in every direction at once, no gap. Too dense to dodge: get behind a fort. Shelter-only, exactly as the host said.
SPECIAL 2, SNOW BOULDERS: 3 giant snowballs roll down 3 lanes drawn in the snow. Each lane is 2.5m wide, so ONE step sideways clears you if you move when the lane appears. This is the only special where a fort isn't the only answer — see the 'two specials, two mistakes' entry.
BOTH SPECIALS ARE INSTANT LOSS if they touch you (host). Neither can be lobbed, so a fort always saves you.
WARNING (host: lots of it): a snowflake swirl gathers around him, bigger and louder each half-second, with a different wind-up pose per special. Burst warning 2.5s (dash to cover). Boulder warning 4.0s (notice the lane, step 1.25m clear) — the slower read needs the longer promise. No special fires without the full swirl.
RHYTHM: one special every ~15s, alternating, never the same kind twice in a row. After each special he's dizzy for 2s (wobbling head): free throws, the reward for surviving (Creative's fumble).
Rule kept: everything visible before it can hit; no homing.

before.title: Decided (Foreman; host's calls outrank everything)
before.text:
- 1 human + 3 AI allies (Pip, Scoop, Waffle) vs 4 AI. Match = first to 2 rounds of 120s (host): your hill, their hill, the park only at 1-1.
- Round: most crown-seconds with the toboggan. Sled starts beside the human in round 1, foot-centre in rounds 2–3. Every crown = same flat saddle. Tie → sudden death, capped 60s.
- Clock: afternoon → dusk (≥4 steps) → streetlights at 120s, plus a 20s countdown. Lighting resets between rounds.
- Camera: one fixed iso shot, whole ~26m hill, kids ~48px at 720p. No pan.
- Controls (host): mouse only. Right-click walks toward the cursor, left-click throws (hands off while carrying), middle-click builds.
- No elimination: a chilled kid warms up at the cocoa stand, ~8s, out of play. Target ≤2 chills per kid per round (bench + siege chills counted together, <15%).
- Garage shop (host, rule 4): 4 credits per round guaranteed + hits + crown time; one purchase per visit; ice 4, melter 4, rock 8, snowman 8, launcher 10; upgrades last the match only. Shop screen may use text. Not yet built: bazooka, igloo, fort.
- Plain snowball = fast flat line, never clears a wall. Wall: one per kid, 1s plant at your feet, 8s cooldown (ghost footprint). Nothing built on the crown.
- Hits: first kid touched below head height in flight, or anyone in the ring at touchdown. One hit chills. No friendly fire.
- AI: Beanie, Pockets (blower), Brick (never throws), Copycat; fair-bot dodging.
- SIEGE: whoever holds the crown faces one shared volley, ONE release frame per cadence, never more than 4 live rings. Defenders 8m+ bracket the carrier's path; closer ones throw one direct shot. Cadence 2.0 / 1.5 / 1.45s per street; street 3 adds a second blower.
- Session: up to 3 named streets (Maple Court, Ivy Terrace, The Summit Kids); nothing carries between streets.

NEXT: Systems builds the siege, reruns the bot log against the 'Host playtest 1' limits, then the host plays again.

summary: edited section “Greybox verdict rules (QA) — decide bef…”

before.title: Greybox verdict rules (QA) — decide before we look
before.text:
Three first-timers, no coaching, one greybox match (first to 2 rounds of 120s, hill A, final camera, full dusk ending, porch screen). Temp audio on: whistle, crunch, sled shout, release, impact, wall break, lights clunk; no sound for a landing ring. No audio = void session.

WATCH, nothing asked: 1) touches the sled within 20s; 2) hands off in the first minute (QA #23); 3) builds unprompted in round 1, and whether a cooldown press stops them; 4) says who's winning at 35s and 105s; 5) porch button + hover time (QA #24); 6) what they look at while carrying (QA #25). Write down the first unprompted complaint verbatim, with the minute.
STOPWATCH: seconds the human can't act (chilled, walking, at the stand; carrying is play). Target <15%; >25% = bench or walk too long.
CSV: human's share of crown-seconds (QA #21); sudden-death rounds (>1 in 6 = scoring too flat); crown vs open-field chills.
AFTER: what told you time was running out (sky or countdown)? How did you know the sled changed hands? Lose sight of sled or kid? What changed the score? Best moment? What did you do when not carrying? Reopen the shop on purpose?

ONE FIX PER FAILURE, agreed now:
- never touches the sled → cut a rule or move a spawn, never a prompt.
- never hands off → fix the ally wave, no text.
- never builds → cut the human's build; Brick keeps his walls.
- stops building after a cooldown press → bolder ghost footprint, no text.
- can't say who's winning → fix the score strip.
- loses the sled → camera or pennant failed; no new HUD.
- not in the score (QA #21) → move the round 2–3 sled toward Chestnut; never slow allies.
- picks 'Finish snow day' → don't shorten the clock. Bucket possession changes by 30s: mostly in the first 60s = fix crown/geometry; late = the ending failed.

n=3 proves confusion, not fun. Fun verdict = the host playing a whole match.

after.title: Greybox verdict rules (QA) — decide before we look
after.text:
Three first-timers, no coaching, one greybox match (first to 2 rounds of 120s, hill A, final camera, full dusk ending, porch screen). Temp audio: whistle, crunch, sled shout, release, impact, wall break, lights clunk; no sound for a landing ring. No audio = void session.

WATCH, nothing asked: 1) touches the sled within 20s; 2) hands off in minute 1 (QA #23); 3) builds unprompted in round 1, and whether a cooldown press stops them; 4) says who's winning at 35s and 105s; 5) porch button + hover time (QA #24); 6) what they look at while carrying (QA #25). Log the first unprompted complaint verbatim, with the minute.
STOPWATCH: seconds the human can't act (chilled, walking, at the stand; carrying counts as play). Target <15%; >25% = bench or walk too long.
CSV: human's crown-second share (QA #21); sudden-death rounds (>1 in 6 = scoring too flat); crown vs open-field chills.
AFTER: What told you time was running out (sky or countdown)? How did you know the sled changed hands? Lose sight of sled or kid? What changed the score? Best moment? What did you do when not carrying? Reopen the shop on purpose?

ONE FIX PER FAILURE:
- never touches the sled → cut a rule or move a spawn, never a prompt.
- never hands off → fix the ally wave, no text.
- never builds → cut the human's build; Brick keeps his walls.
- stops building after a cooldown press → bolder ghost footprint, no text.
- can't say who's winning → fix the score strip.
- loses the sled → camera or pennant failed; no new HUD.
- not in the score → move the round 2–3 sled toward Chestnut; never slow allies.
- picks 'Finish snow day' → don't shorten the clock. Bucket possession changes by 30s: mostly in the first 60s = fix crown/geometry; late = the ending failed.

n=3 proves confusion, not fun. Fun verdict = the host playing a whole match.

before.text:

PRICES: ice 4, melter 4, rock 8, snowman 8, launcher 10. Cheapest = 4 = a no-hit, no-crown round, so the shelf is never bare (QA #28).

before.label: 7. Throwing: aim a spot, hard line
before.text:
Mouse aims a landing ring (r 0.8m); left-click throws. Ring visible to all from commitment; ball casts a shadow dot. Your own ring hides while you carry; the handoff outline replaces it (QA #25).
- Plain: 0.35s + 0.05s/m, flat, 12m, NEVER clears a wall.
- Ice: 0.25s + 0.03s/m, flat, 12m, shatters the wall it hits.
- Rock: plain flight (0.35s + 0.05s/m, 12m) but smashes through walls and snowmen and keeps going; a kid it chills is knocked 1.5m off the spot, so a carrier lands away from the sled they dropped.
- Launcher: hold to spray pellets: 0.3s + 0.04s/m, 9m, ring 0.45m, scatter up to 0.5m, 15-ball hopper, 2.5s reload when empty. One pellet chills, same as a ball; balance it by price and the shop gate, not by a damage system.
- Melter: walking into a rival wall or snowman melts it; touching a chilled teammate thaws them instantly (once per 6s). Host's call: this restores the ruled-out 'heal a chilled ally' idea.
- Snowman: your build button makes a snowman instead of a wall (3 hits to break, 12s cooldown); it pelts rivals within 8m every 2.2s.
- Blower (Pockets): 0.50s + 0.12s/m, high lob, clears walls, 14m.

before.label: Behaviour rules (Systems) — no state trees
before.text:
Beanie: grabs a free sled, shortest legal path to the crown. Throws only when the sled has been off the crown 5s+. Never builds.
Pockets: blower only; holds 6–10m from the nearest enemy, faces their carrier, backs off inside 6m. Carries only as fallback.
Brick: never carries, receives or throws. Keeps his wall between his carrier and the nearest threat (outside the crown, ≥2m from the sled); wall down = walks 2m ahead as a shield.
Copycat: 2s after the human acts, repeats that action type; never initiates (copies the stand-in in bot runs).
SIEGE suspends Beanie's 5s rule and Copycat's never-initiate rule (Host playtest 1).
FAIR-BOT: reacts only to committed rings in its ~120° front arc, after its reaction time, by walking 0.8m out (rule 11). Carriers and builders don't dodge.
Difficulty = street tier (rule 10); reaction 0.45–0.60s governs dodging only. Fallback carrier when Beanie is chilled 3s+: Pockets, then Copycat.
ALLIES: same logic. They never take a handoff the human didn't give, but a sled the human drops is free for anyone, allies included (6b stays ruled out).
SHOPPING: wishlists in rule 4.
STAND-IN (bot runs): Beanie logic, plain snowballs; in shop tests buys the item under test.

before.label: Fix 2: Bracket — lead from range, one direct shot up close, one release frame
before.text:
One volley = every free thrower's ring on the SAME frame (rule 10 lists them per street).
FAR (8m+) plain rings: lead = carrier position + velocity × flight time; a second plain ring sits 1.2m to one side of the lead.
NEAR (<8m): one direct shot at the carrier's position, no lead, same frame.
CAPPERS (Pockets' blowers) land ~1s late on the obvious exit; on street 3 two cappers cover both exits.
The bracket punishes running straight, the near shot punishes standing still, the capper punishes the obvious exit. Irregular walking is the skill. Walking out of a ring inside the 4m crown keeps you scoring.
Handoff is the free escape: the volley lands where the sled was. All rings visible from release, no homing.

object.author: claude
object.title: Boss bout: Frosty (merged spec, Foreman + Systems + QA)

entries.label: Frosty: 60s, 10 hits to melt, you can take 3 (host)
entries.text: Your kid alone against Frosty on the same hill, 60s, streetlights on. Frosty sits on the crown, never moves or dodges, and is big and easy to hit. He needs 10 hits to melt; you go down after 3. A hit on you = knockback + cancelled throw, never the cocoa stand. His 3rd hit on you, or the clock, ends it. You have plain snowballs plus whatever you bought.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Frosty's attacks: normal throws + 2 specials (host)
entries.text:
NORMAL: aimed siege volleys at you (lead ring + direct ring + lob). A hit = one of your 3.
SPECIAL 1, BLIZZARD BURST: a full ring of 24 flat snowballs in every direction at once, no gap. Too dense to dodge: get behind a fort. Shelter-only, exactly as the host said.
SPECIAL 2, SNOW BOULDERS: 3 giant snowballs roll down 3 lanes drawn in the snow. Each lane is 2.5m wide, so ONE step sideways clears you if you move when the lane appears. This is the only special where a fort isn't the only answer — see the 'two specials, two mistakes' entry.
BOTH SPECIALS ARE INSTANT LOSS if they touch you (host). Neither can be lobbed, so a fort always saves you.
WARNING (host: lots of it): a snowflake swirl gathers around him, bigger and louder each half-second, with a different wind-up pose per special. Burst warning 2.5s (dash to cover). Boulder warning 4.0s (notice the lane, step 1.25m clear) — the slower read needs the longer promise. No special fires without the full swirl.
RHYTHM: one special every ~15s, alternating, never the same kind twice in a row. After each special he's dizzy for 2s (wobbling head): free throws, the reward for surviving (Creative's fumble).
Rule kept: everything visible before it can hit; no homing.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Shelter: four snow forts around the crown (host)
entries.text: Four fixed waist-high snow forts, ~7m from Frosty in a square, with gaps between them. They never break: a burst hits all four at once, so crumbling forts would make the third special unsurvivable. They block everything flat: normal volleys, the burst and the boulders. They don't block his normal lob, so camping still costs you hits. Your plain snowballs can't clear a fort, so you must step out to throw. Your own build button adds one more wall.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Prize: porch trophy, never credits or power (Systems conceded)
entries.text:
Systems' free-item prize is withdrawn; this is now the trophy. Win: Frosty's pot hat sits on your porch snowman for the rest of the snow day, plus the porch line 'You melted Frosty'.
WHY the trophy and not power: Frosty never dodges, so every accurate throw hits — 10 hits costs ~20s of good throwing, which means the bout is close to a guaranteed win. A near-guaranteed win that pays a free item hands out a launcher-class item for showing up, and perturbs the 4/8/10 ladder and the street tier we just tuned. A trophy pays nothing mechanical, so it can be won every match without touching balance. (Creative and Art asked for this; they were right.)
Revisit only if the bot log shows the bout is genuinely losable for a first-timer.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Losing costs nothing
entries.text: Frosty slumps back to sleep. No credits or items lost; the bout is a bonus, never a tax.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Placement: 'Next street' plays it, 'Finish' skips it
entries.text: The bout sits after the porch screen (QA), so it never delays the Next/Finish read (#24). 'Next street' or 'New snow day' plays the bout, then the next whistle; 'Finish snow day' skips it. No third button. WATCH: if players who chose Next still quit during the bout, shorten it before adding anything.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Special choreography — warning is a promise (Creative proposal)
entries.text: Pause normal throws for the full special warning, release and recovery; begin the warning only after earlier lobs have landed. Otherwise a lob can evict you from the shelter the instant-loss attack demands. Burst pose: arms spread, snowflakes orbit his belly. Boulder pose: crouch, gather snow between both mittens. Keep flakes close to Frosty so the route and fort edges stay visible. Start the 2s head-fumble recovery after the special has passed the shelters, not at release.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=creative

entries.label: Lose the bout, not the cozy tone (Creative proposal)
entries.text: An instant-loss hit leaves a kid-shaped snowdrift; the human's hat pops out, then a mitten. No death pose or injury. On victory Frosty slumps into a little heap with his pot on top. Both endings should be quick visual punchlines, not another results screen.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=creative

entries.label: Two specials, two different mistakes (answers Creative's challenge)
entries.text:
If both specials are answered by 'be behind a fort', the second one is a reskin: same input, same result, twice the art. So the pair is split by how you fail:
- BURST (2.5s, radial, no gap) = you were too far from cover when it started. Mistake: out of position.
- BOULDERS (4.0s, three 2.5m lanes) = you stood still in a marked lane, or you were mid-commit and couldn't move (rule 13). Mistake: didn't read the lane / threw at the wrong time.
Both still leave the fort as the safe answer, so the host's instant-loss-unless-sheltered rule is untouched for the burst; the boulder is the one attack where the drawn lane is also a legal answer, which is the only reason it exists.
IF the host wants the boulder shelter-only too: make each lane 6m wide so the three span the hill and there is no strip to stand in. Accept that the two specials are then one attack in two costumes, and expect to cut one after the first playtest.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Hit budget: the clock is not the constraint, so tune specials first
entries.text:
The arithmetic for 60s / 10 hits, plain ball (0.85s flight at 10m), one throw per 0.6s:
60s − 3 specials × (2.5–4.0s warning + ~1s release + 2s dizzy) ≈ 21s of special, of which ~6s dizzy is free throwing → ~45s of throwing, ~75 throws, 10 needed. Against a static target that never dodges that is a ~13% accuracy requirement: 10 hits is a pacing device, not a skill test. Good — it means a first-timer normally wins, which is why the prize must be cosmetic.
The fail state is therefore entirely the specials and his normal volleys. TUNING ORDER if the bout is too easy or too hard: 1) special frequency (15s → 12/18s), 2) hits to melt (10 → 8/12), 3) fort distance from Frosty. Never the 60s clock and never the 2.5/4.0s warnings — the warnings are the fairness promise, not a difficulty dial.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Art fairness gate — shelter is geometry, not a particle count
entries.text: 24 discrete balls do not prove a gapless burst; validate projectile width/spacing at the farthest playable radius. Any collision envelope must match the visible snow, never invisible damage between balls. Freeze warning clips at 720p: first-timer points to safe side of fort, then reaches it with right-click before release from the worst legal position. Include acceleration/path around fort, not just straight-line distance. Host asked both specials to require shelter: sidestep-safe boulders remain an unapproved exception, not a settled rule.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: The warning is longer than the arena — the instant loss can't fire
entries.text:
2.5s at 4.5 m/s buys 11m of running. The forts sit ~7m out on a ~26m hill, so a kid who reads the flakes even once is behind cover every time and the instant loss never happens.

So the special's real job, per the arithmetic, is a TIME TAX: 3 × (2.5s warning + ~1s release + 2s dizzy) ≈ 16.5s, a quarter of a 60s bout spent walking to a rock and back. Survivable, but not a decision.

Don't shorten the warnings — they're the fairness promise. Pick one:
- SPREAD the forts so the safe side is 8m+ from where a good thrower wants to stand: the dash becomes a route, not a twitch; or
- accept the time tax and CUT to one special if the log shows zero instant losses.

FREE FROM THE LOG: per bout, distance to nearest shelter at warning start, seconds to reach it, and whether the special killed. 10 bouts, no deaths = the warning IS the attack.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: The trophy is invisible — nothing on screen shows it
entries.text:
Every version of the prize now ends as Frosty's pot hat "on your porch snowman for the rest of the snow day", but the porch screen is two lines of text and the only snowman object in the game is a bought build item. As written, you win the trophy and never see it again.

CHEAP FIX: a small snowman wearing the pot stands at the foot of YOUR porch, on the field, in every later round of the snow day. Static, low, no pennant, never near the crown — it must never be readable as scoring (history stays off the crown, per the ruled-out pennant). Then "I melted him" is something a kid points at, not a line they read.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: Hold the boss art until the base loop passes one gate
entries.text:
No siege in the prototype, no bot log, no human match since the host's complaint. The bout now has 13 entries, two concept sheets, a new HUD that replaces the score strip and a death animation.

RULE: no boss art, no boss HUD, no bout code until the siege log passes (median crown hold 8–20s over ≥12 holds). A 60s boss standing on the same hill inherits whatever is wrong with the crown, and with one witness instead of eight it will look like it works.

entries.label: Two specials, two different mistakes (answers Creative's challenge)
entries.text:
If both specials are answered by 'be behind a fort', the second one is a reskin: same input, same result, twice the art. So the pair is split by how you fail:
- BURST (2.5s, radial, no gap) = you were too far from cover when it started. Mistake: out of position.
- BOULDERS (4.0s, three 2.5m lanes) = you stood still in a marked lane, or you were mid-commit and couldn't move (rule 13). Mistake: didn't read the lane / threw at the wrong time.
Both still leave the fort as the safe answer, so the host's instant-loss-unless-sheltered rule is untouched for the burst; the boulder is the one attack where the drawn lane is also a legal answer, which is the only reason it exists.
IF the host wants the boulder shelter-only too: make each lane 6m wide so the three span the hill and there is no strip to stand in. Accept that the two specials are then one attack in two costumes, and expect to cut one after the first playtest.

entries.label: Hit budget: the clock is not the constraint, so tune specials first
entries.text:
The arithmetic for 60s / 10 hits, plain ball (0.85s flight at 10m), one throw per 0.6s:
60s − 3 specials × (2.5–4.0s warning + ~1s release + 2s dizzy) ≈ 21s of special, of which ~6s dizzy is free throwing → ~45s of throwing, ~75 throws, 10 needed. Against a static target that never dodges that is a ~13% accuracy requirement: 10 hits is a pacing device, not a skill test. Good — it means a first-timer normally wins, which is why the prize must be cosmetic.
The fail state is therefore entirely the specials and his normal volleys. TUNING ORDER if the bout is too easy or too hard: 1) special frequency (15s → 12/18s), 2) hits to melt (10 → 8/12), 3) fort distance from Frosty. Never the 60s clock and never the 2.5/4.0s warnings — the warnings are the fairness promise, not a difficulty dial.

entries.label: Art fairness gate — shelter is geometry, not a particle count

Any collision envelope must match the visible snow, never invisible damage between balls. Freeze warning clips at 720p: first-timer points to safe side of fort, then reaches it with right-click before release from the worst legal position. Include acceleration/path around fort, not just straight-line distance. Host asked both specials to require shelter: sidestep-safe boulders remain an unapproved exception, not a settled rule.

- accept the time tax and CUT to one special if the log shows zero instant losses.

FREE FROM THE LOG: per bout, distance to nearest shelter at warning start, seconds to reach it, and whether the special killed. 10 bouts, no deaths = the warning IS the attack.

before.label: Frosty's attacks: normal throws + 2 specials (host)
before.text:
NORMAL: aimed siege volleys at you (lead ring + direct ring + lob). A hit = one of your 3.
SPECIAL 1, BLIZZARD BURST: a full ring of 24 flat snowballs in every direction at once, no gap. Too dense to dodge: get behind a fort. Shelter-only, exactly as the host said.
SPECIAL 2, SNOW BOULDERS: 3 giant snowballs roll down 3 lanes drawn in the snow. Each lane is 2.5m wide, so ONE step sideways clears you if you move when the lane appears. This is the only special where a fort isn't the only answer — see the 'two specials, two mistakes' entry.
BOTH SPECIALS ARE INSTANT LOSS if they touch you (host). Neither can be lobbed, so a fort always saves you.
WARNING (host: lots of it): a snowflake swirl gathers around him, bigger and louder each half-second, with a different wind-up pose per special. Burst warning 2.5s (dash to cover). Boulder warning 4.0s (notice the lane, step 1.25m clear) — the slower read needs the longer promise. No special fires without the full swirl.
RHYTHM: one special every ~15s, alternating, never the same kind twice in a row. After each special he's dizzy for 2s (wobbling head): free throws, the reward for surviving (Creative's fumble).
Rule kept: everything visible before it can hit; no homing.

before.title: Decided (Foreman; host's calls outrank everything)
before.text:
- 1 human + 3 AI allies (Pip, Scoop, Waffle) vs 4 AI. Match = first to 2 rounds of 120s (host): your hill, their hill, the park only at 1-1.
- Round: most crown-seconds with the toboggan. Sled starts beside the human in round 1, foot-centre in rounds 2–3. Every crown = same flat saddle. Tie → sudden death, capped 60s.
- Clock: afternoon → dusk (≥4 steps) → streetlights at 120s, plus a 20s countdown. Lighting resets each round.
- Camera: one fixed iso shot of the whole ~26m hill, kids ~48px at 720p. No pan.
- Controls (host): mouse only. Right-click walks to the cursor, left-click throws (hands off while carrying), middle-click builds.
- No elimination: a chilled kid warms up at the cocoa stand, ~8s, out of play. Target ≤2 chills per kid per round (bench + siege combined, <15%).
- Garage shop (host, rule 4): 4 credits/round guaranteed + hits + crown time; one purchase per visit; ice 4, melter 4, rock 8, snowman 8, launcher 10; upgrades last the match only. Shop screen may use text. Not yet built: bazooka, igloo, fort.
- Plain snowball = fast flat line, never clears a wall. Wall: one per kid, 1s plant at your feet, 8s cooldown (ghost footprint). Nothing built on the crown.
- Hits: first kid touched below head height in flight, or anyone in the ring at touchdown. One hit chills. No friendly fire.
- AI: Beanie, Pockets (blower), Brick (never throws), Copycat; fair-bot dodging.
- SIEGE: the crown holder faces one shared volley, ONE release frame per cadence, ≤4 live rings. Defenders 8m+ bracket the carrier's path; closer ones throw one direct shot. Cadence 2.0 / 1.5 / 1.45s per street; street 3 adds a second blower.
- Session: up to 3 named streets (Maple Court, Ivy Terrace, The Summit Kids); nothing carries between streets.

NEXT: Systems builds the siege, reruns the bot log against the 'Host playtest 1' limits, then the host plays again.

before.title: Decided (Foreman; host's calls outrank everything)
before.text:

- Round: most crown-seconds with the toboggan. Sled starts beside the human in round 1, foot-centre in rounds 2–3. Every crown = same flat saddle. Tie → sudden death, capped 60s.

- Camera: one fixed iso shot of the whole ~26m hill, kids ~48px at 720p. No pan.

after.label: 32. Persisting powerups — the cost isn't rules, it's the ladder
after.text:
VARIANT to test before the host rules: items persist across the 3 streets of one snow day, but the 4-credit/round guarantee and savings carry-over are dropped from streets 2–3, and it all wipes at 'New snow day'. One purchase per visit stays.
WHY: street cadence is fixed (2.0 → 1.5 → 1.45s), so a persistent kit against a fixed ladder means a player who won street 1 gets street 3 easier and a player who lost gets it harder — the opposite of the ladder's job. Persistence should be savings, not free power.
WATCH: street 2 and 3 win rate vs street 1 (a >20pt jump = the day is inverted); first-timers' "what do I still have?" question at the street-2 whistle; and per-item win rate again — Launcher is the first suspect when it's live for three streets instead of one.
FROSTY: if the host rules persistence, the bout's 'plain snowballs only, no building' needs its own reason (it's a bonus bout, the host's rule) — it can no longer cite rule 4, or it reads as an arbitrary exception.

after.label: Do upgrades persist across streets? (host's question, Systems)
after.text:
Default stays: upgrades last one match (2–3 rounds). Persisting across all 3 streets has three costs, one of them already ruled on.
1) THE PRICE TRIPLES, THE GOODS DON'T. Credits reset per match, so a 10-credit launcher bought at street 2 would pay for streets 2 and 3 for one price. The one real shop decision (cheap now vs save for the launcher) collapses into 'always save for the biggest thing, it lasts forever'. A persistent launcher at 40–60% win rate in a match becomes >60% over a snow day — it's the first item the win-rate gate would flag.
2) THE LADDER INVERTS. Street 3 exists to be harder (cadence 2.0 → 1.45s, second blower, reaction 0.45s). Your kit rising on the same axis cancels it, and we'd have to retune all three streets against accumulated kits instead of against plain snowballs.
3) THE EXIT GETS EXPENSIVE. QA #26 ruled out unlocks across snow days because they make 'Finish snow day' cost something. Persisting across streets is that same failure one level down: quitting mid-snow-day throws away your kit, which poisons the 'Next street' vs 'Finish' read (#24).
IF THE HOST WANTS THE FEEL, the cheap version is a per-item flag, not a retune: persist what does not compound — ice (4) and melter (4) and rock (8) are one-shot power; reset what compounds — snowman (8, a structure that fights every round) and launcher (10, 15 pellets every round). Same cozy sense of a growing kit, no ladder retune, and the launcher keeps its save-up decision. Cost: one field in the shop data.
TEST either version on a 3-street horizon: the per-item win-rate gate (30+ matches) run per street instead of per match. Outside 40–60% on any single street = too strong once persisted.

after.label: Equip slots: owning everything must not stack everything (Systems)
after.text:
With gear persisting, income is ~20 credits a match and the whole shelf is 36, so by street 2–3 every kid owns every item. If ownership stacks, street 3 is eight kids carrying launchers and snowmen: the field breaks QA #29's ≤4 live rings and the 1.2m miss rule, and the shop has no decisions left after half a snow day.
FIX, and it needs no new items (Creative is right not to fill the shelf yet): a kid CARRIES one throw and one build replacement. Ice and rock already share one slot, the snowman already replaces the wall — so make it explicit that owning the launcher does not delete the plain ball, you choose which throw you carry. Swapping is FREE in the garage and uses the same visit, so a street-3 visit becomes 'which two for this hill' (melter or snowman against street 3's two blowers). Your collection persists; your loadout is two of it. That is also Art's owned-vs-equipped distinction, with a slot strip in the garage.
SIEGE IMMUNITY: a siege volley always uses the street's listed rings (rule 10), never a bot's purchased item. Rule 4 already promises rival purchases never change the street tier; this keeps that true and keeps the ≤4 ring cap honest once every bot owns a launcher. Bot gear still counts in the open field, which is where it was bought for.
TEST: log swaps per shop visit on streets 2–3. Zero swaps once items are owned = the late shop is a dead screen, and that is the signal to fill the shelf — not before.

after.label: Persistence: the number that breaks isn't win rate (Systems)
after.text:
A 20-point win-rate jump on streets 2–3 is a weak detector: the bots buy gear too, so the swing partly cancels, and n=3 sessions can't see 20 points anyway. The number that actually moves when every kid owns a launcher is CHILLS, and it is already gated — 4–8 per team per round, ≤2 per kid (rule 4/bench, QA #31). Gear that persists raises open-field lethality for everyone, so the first symptom of a kit that has outgrown the rules is street 3 at 4+ chills per kid, which breaks the no-elimination feel and the <15% bench line long before it moves a win rate.
SO: read chills per kid per round street by street (street 1 = the baseline the same player just set), plus crown-hold median (siege Gate: 8–20s). Launch launcher-driven chills apart from plain-ball ones in the CSV — the launcher is the only item where one purchase compounds every round.
TWO SINKS, cheapest first: 1) if a garage visit has nothing left to sell, make it ONE click that skips to the next hill (Creative: don't invent a decision to keep the screen busy) — never a tour of things you own; 2) only then the two-slot loadout, which is the lever Foreman named. Price rises and street retuning are the wrong levers: one is invisible and the other fights a kit that grows all day.

after.label: 35. Fallback trigger: 'zero swaps' is a tautology — use the chill gate per street
after.text:
THE 'NOBODY SWAPS GEAR' TRIGGER CANNOT FIRE. Swapping isn't a decision in the shop today: the only replaceable pair is ice↔rock, and that swap is a mistake, not a choice. The condition is created by the fix it's supposed to trigger.
REPLACE BOTH TRIGGERS with the gate we already have, read per street: street 3 chills per kid breaks the ruled ≤2 (or bench >15%) while the same child's street 1 clears it. Lifeless open-field lethality shows up as chills, not as a win-rate delta three sessions can't resolve. Split launcher chills out in the CSV — it's the only item that compounds every round.
AND the dead visit is a test, not a debate: log garage visits per street. Nothing bought and nothing useful to say = the visit is one click that skips to the next hill (calls Agree: Art/Systems). Zero swaps is only evidence once swapping exists.
